<script>
// Zoom controls for large figures: any <div class="zoomable"> gets a toolbar
// (−, +, reset, fit) and a scrollable viewport; the image is scaled with CSS transforms.
(function () {
  function setup(box) {
    var img = box.querySelector('img');
    if (!img) return;
    var vp = document.createElement('div'); vp.className = 'zoom-viewport';
    while (box.firstChild) vp.appendChild(box.firstChild);
    var bar = document.createElement('div'); bar.className = 'zoom-toolbar';
    var scale = 1, label = document.createElement('span');
    function apply() {
      img.style.transform = 'scale(' + scale + ')';
      img.style.width = '100%';
      vp.style.height = scale > 1 ? '85vh' : '';
      label.textContent = Math.round(scale * 100) + '%';
    }
    function mk(txt, fn, title) {
      var b = document.createElement('button'); b.className = 'btn btn-default btn-xs';
      b.textContent = txt; b.title = title; b.addEventListener('click', fn); return b;
    }
    bar.appendChild(mk('\u2212', function () { scale = Math.max(0.25, scale / 1.25); apply(); }, 'Zoom out'));
    bar.appendChild(mk('+', function () { scale = Math.min(8, scale * 1.25); apply(); }, 'Zoom in'));
    bar.appendChild(mk('Reset', function () { scale = 1; apply(); vp.scrollTop = 0; vp.scrollLeft = 0; }, 'Fit to column'));
    bar.appendChild(label);
    var hint = document.createElement('span'); hint.style.marginLeft = 'auto';
    hint.textContent = 'Scroll inside the frame to pan when zoomed';
    bar.appendChild(hint);
    box.appendChild(bar); box.appendChild(vp);
    apply();
  }
  function start() { document.querySelectorAll('.zoomable').forEach(setup); }
  if (document.readyState === 'complete') start(); else window.addEventListener('load', start);
})();
</script>

<script>
// Relabel the per-chunk code-folding buttons. rmarkdown's own script creates the
// buttons after page load and rewrites their text ("Code"/"Hide") on every
// toggle, so a MutationObserver re-applies the explicit labels whenever that happens.
(function () {
  var MAP = { 'Code': 'Show code', 'Hide': 'Hide code' };
  function relabel() {
    var btns = document.querySelectorAll('.code-folding-btn');
    for (var i = 0; i < btns.length; i++) {
      var t = btns[i].textContent.trim();
      if (MAP[t]) btns[i].textContent = MAP[t];
    }
  }
  function start() {
    relabel();
    var obs = new MutationObserver(function () { relabel(); });
    obs.observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true, characterData: true });
  }
  if (document.readyState === 'complete') start();
  else window.addEventListener('load', start);
})();
</script>

<p class="ms-abstract-head">Abstract</p>

<p class="ms-abstract">Genetic medicine has become a routine component of clinical care, yet the evidence guiding its implementation remains heavily weighted toward pediatric populations, with limited practice-level data to inform adult referral pathways, test selection, or service delivery. We analyzed eight years of electronic health record (EHR)-linked data from a high-volume adult genetics clinic (9,867 visits) within a major academic health system to define referral patterns, test utilization, and genetic testing outcomes across indications and demographic groups. While most visits were in-person and led by a genetics-trained physician, genetic counselor-only visits accounted for 12% of all encounters and telemedicine remained a substantial component of follow-up care, comprising 39% of follow-up visits from 2023 onward. Genetic testing was ordered for 52% of all new patients, with significant indication-specific variation in ordering propensity. Overall, 24% of all tests returned a diagnostic result. Diagnostic yield differed markedly by testing modality: exome sequencing yielded diagnoses in 40% of patients, whereas next-generation sequencing panels, the most frequently ordered testing type, yielded diagnoses in only 16%. Although diagnostic yield declined with increasing patient age, it remained above 17% in every age stratum, with the yield of exome/genome sequencing remaining above 30% across all age groups. Outcomes varied significantly by referral indication, with some indications yielding significantly high rates of pathogenic findings, and others more often yielding negative or uncertain results. Operational factors significantly shaped practice: test type and laboratory utilization shifted significantly over time in step with payer and testing lab policy changes. Together, these practice-based data establish adult genetics as a high-yield and important clinical domain. Our findings provide actionable evidence to inform age- and indication-aware triage, guide workforce planning, promote adult-focused practice guidelines, better inform payor reimbursement policies, and advance the integration of genomic medicine into routine adult patient care.</p>

## Setup: data path and API key {#setup}

<div class="note">
<strong>Nothing private is stored in this document.</strong> The notebook reads two values from environment variables at knit time; the values themselves never appear in the Rmd or the HTML.
<ul>
<li><code>MEDGEN_DATA_PATH</code> – full path to the cleaned clinic data used in the analyses.</li>
<li><code>STADIA_MAPS_KEY</code> – your Stadia Maps API key, used only for the Figure 1A base map.</li>
</ul>
To set them once per machine: run <code>usethis::edit_r_environ()</code> (or open <code>~/.Renviron</code> in any editor), add the two lines below, save, then <strong>restart R</strong>:
<pre>MEDGEN_DATA_PATH=path-to-data
STADIA_MAPS_KEY=your-key-here</pre>
If you prefer a project-level file, put the same two lines in a <code>.Renviron</code> file next to this Rmd and add <code>.Renviron</code> to <code>.gitignore</code>. The chunks below stop with a clear message if either variable is missing.

## Data loading and recoding {#data}

<details class="code">
<summary>Libraries, data import, age ranges, race/ethnicity categories, indication-group recoding</summary>

```{r helpers}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Shared helper functions (defined once here; previously re-defined in six
## separate statistics chunks).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Collapse the raw EHR race labels into the analysis categories used throughout.
recode_race <- function(race) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    race %in% c("Some Other Race", "Unknown", "Patient Declined", "Other") ~ "Unknown/Other",
    race %in% c("Black", "HLB-Hispanic Latino/Black")                       ~ "Black or African American",
    race == "American Indian"                                                ~ "American Indian or Alaskan Native",
    race == "Pacific Island"                                                 ~ "Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander",
    race == "East Indian"                                                    ~ "Asian",
    race == "HLW-Hispanic Latino/White"                                      ~ "White",
    TRUE                                                                     ~ race
  )
}

# Collapse the many EHR financial-class labels into four analysis categories.
collapse_insurance <- function(fin_class) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    fin_class %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
    fin_class %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare")                             ~ "Medicare",
    fin_class %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)")                        ~ "Medicaid",
    fin_class == "Self-Pay"                                                      ~ "Self-Pay",
    TRUE                                                                         ~ "Other"
  )
}
```

```{r load-data, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Build (output hidden)]  Overview
## What    : Prepares data and builds plot/table objects that are printed in the panel sections below.
## Creates : medgen_data_path, MedGenRawData2025, start_all, end_all, breaks_6mo, MedGenData, MedGenData_Visits, MedGenData_Indications
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(readxl)
library(ggmap)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggnewscale)
library(patchwork)    # for inset_element()
library(scales)      # for comma(), squish()
library(pals)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(DT)
library(plotly)
library(htmltools)
library(broom)
library(corrplot)
library(nnet)
library(kableExtra)
library(emmeans)
library(car)      # previously loaded mid-document
library(knitr)      # previously loaded mid-document

# ---- Input data -------------------------------------------------------------
# The path to the cleaned clinic data is read from the
# MEDGEN_DATA_PATH environment variable so that no local path is stored in this
# document. See the "Setup" box at the top of the notebook.
medgen_data_path <- Sys.getenv("MEDGEN_DATA_PATH")
if (!nzchar(medgen_data_path) || !file.exists(medgen_data_path)) {
  stop("MEDGEN_DATA_PATH is not set or does not point to an existing file. ",
       "Add it to your .Renviron (see the Setup box) and restart R.")
}
MedGenRawData2025 <- readxl::read_xlsx(medgen_data_path)

MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE <- as.Date(MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE_MONTH <- cut(MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE, breaks='quarter')
MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE_YEAR <- cut(MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE, breaks='year')

# Find the full range, snapped to January 1 and July 1
start_all <- floor_date(min(MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE, na.rm = TRUE), "year")
end_all   <- ceiling_date(max(MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE, na.rm = TRUE), "year")

# Create a sequence of 6-month breaks: Jan 1, Jul 1, Jan 1, Jul 1, …
breaks_6mo <- seq(from = start_all, to = end_all, by = "6 months")

MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  mutate(
    half_idx = findInterval(CONTACT_DATE, breaks_6mo, rightmost.closed = FALSE),
    half_idx = ifelse(half_idx == 0, 1, half_idx),
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF = breaks_6mo[half_idx]
  ) %>%
  select(-half_idx)

    # Set actual break points
   breaks_6mo <- sort(unique(MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE_HALF))

# 5. (Optional) If you also want a human‐readable label like “Jan 2016” / “Jul 2016”:
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  mutate(
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF_LABEL = format(CONTACT_DATE_HALF, "%b %Y"))

# Create Age Ranges

MedGenRawData2025$AGE_RANGE <- cut(MedGenRawData2025$VISIT_AGE, breaks = c(0, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 120))

# Create race/ethnicity categories:
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(RACE != "?" & !is.na(RACE) & RACE != "NA") %>%
  mutate(RACE2 = recode_race(RACE)) %>%          # recode_race() is defined in the "helpers" chunk

    filter(ETHNICITY != "?" & !is.na(ETHNICITY) & ETHNICITY != "NA") %>%
  mutate(ETHNICITY2 = ifelse(ETHNICITY == "Hispanic Latino", "Hispanic Latino", "Non-Hispanic Latino")) %>%
  mutate(ETHNICITY2 = ifelse(RACE %in% c("HLB-Hispanic Latino/Black", "HLW-Hispanic Latino/White"), "Hispanic Latino", ETHNICITY2)) %>%
  mutate(RACE = ifelse(ETHNICITY2 == "Hispanic Latino", "Hispanic or Latino of any race", RACE2))

# Update Indication Groups and gene typos
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication.Group = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "von Hippel Lindau syndrome", "Cancer genetics", Indication.Group))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication.Group = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Weill-Marchesani syndrome", "Connective tissue disorder", Indication.Group))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication.Group = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Camurati Engelmann syndrome", "Connective tissue disorder", Indication.Group))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication.Group = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Brain small vessel disease", "Neuromuscular disorder", Indication.Group))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication.Group = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia", "Bone/Skeletal disorder", Indication.Group))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication.Group = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Hyperparathyroidism", "Endocrine disorder", Indication.Group))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication.Group = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Trichorhinophalangeal syndrome", "Multisystem disorder", Indication.Group))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication_Cleaned = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Carrier Screening", "Carrier screening", Indication_Cleaned))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication_Cleaned = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Biotinidase Deficiency", "Biotinidase deficiency", Indication_Cleaned))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication_Cleaned = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Genetic Counseling", "Genetic counseling", Indication_Cleaned))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication_Cleaned = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Methylmalonic Acidemia", "Methylmalonic acidemia", Indication_Cleaned))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Indication_Cleaned = ifelse(Indication_Cleaned == "Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency", "Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency", Indication_Cleaned))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Gene = ifelse(Gene == "TSC", "TSC1", Gene))
MedGenRawData2025 <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% mutate(Gene = ifelse(Gene == "TAFAZZIN", "TAZ", Gene))

# ---- Analysis datasets (built once; previously rebuilt from the raw data at
# ---- several points in the notebook) -----------------------------------------
#
# MedGenData             all visits after the recoding above (Figures 1, 2A-B, 7, S3, S4)
# MedGenData_Visits      visits with a known sex and indication group, with a
#                        4-level VisitType (Figures 2C-F, S1)
# MedGenData_Indications visits with a cleaned specific indication and an
#                        indication group (Figures 3-6, S2, Table S1)
MedGenData <- MedGenRawData2025

MedGenData_Visits <- MedGenData %>%
  filter(GENDER != "X") %>%
  filter(Indication.Group != "NA") %>%
  mutate(
    VisitType = case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RETURN PATIENT VISIT") ~ "Follow up",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP == "NEW PATIENT VISIT"                                ~ "New patient visit",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP == "NPV TELEHEALTH"                                   ~ "New patient visit, telehealth",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP == "RPV TELEHEALTH"                                   ~ "Follow up, telehealth",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Indication.Group = as.factor(Indication.Group)
  )

MedGenData_Indications <- as.data.frame(
  MedGenData %>%
    filter(Indication_Cleaned != "NA") %>%
    filter(Indication.Group != "NA")
)
```

## 1A · Heatmap of patient home addresses {#fig1a}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Heatmap of patient home addresses over a map of the Delaware Valley, with major cities labeled. The inset magnifies the City of Philadelphia. Color indicates the number of unique patient visits per hexagonal unit.</div>

```{r heatmap, fig.width=9, fig.height=8.5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 1 > 1A · Heatmap of patient home addresses
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : stadia_key, MedGenMapData, map1.background, map1.labels, map2.background, map2.labels, Hex.Map.Big, Hex.Map.Small, small_map_framed, final_plot
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------
# Full R script to generate the inset hex‐maps
# ---------------------------------------------

# 2. Register your Stadia Maps API key (if not already done in this session)
stadia_key <- Sys.getenv("STADIA_MAPS_KEY")
if (!nzchar(stadia_key)) {
  stop("STADIA_MAPS_KEY is not set. Add it to your .Renviron (see the Setup box) and restart R.")
}
register_stadiamaps(key = stadia_key, write = FALSE)

# 3. Define (or load) your point‐data

MedGenMapData <- MedGenRawData2025

# ---------------------------------------------
# 4. Fetch the base maps using get_stadiamap()
# ---------------------------------------------

# 4a. Big map: covers roughly PA/NJ/MD/DE region
map1.background <- get_stadiamap(
  bbox    = c(left   = -77.7,
              bottom =  38.5,
              right  = -73.7,
              top    =  41.8),
  maptype = "stamen_terrain_background",
  zoom    = 10,
  scale   = 2
)

map1.labels <- get_stadiamap(
  bbox    = c(left   = -77.7,
              bottom =  38.5,
              right  = -73.7,
              top    =  41.8),
  maptype = "stamen_terrain_labels",
  zoom    = 10,
  scale   = 2
)

# 4b. Small map: zoomed into a subregion near Philadelphia
map2.background <- get_stadiamap(
  bbox    = c(left   = -75.335,
              bottom =  39.86,
              right  = -75.02,
              top    =  40.095),
  maptype = "stamen_terrain_background",
  zoom    = 14,
  scale   = 2
)

map2.labels <- get_stadiamap(
  bbox    = c(left   = -75.335,
              bottom =  39.86,
              right  = -75.02,
              top    =  40.095),
  maptype = "stamen_terrain_labels",
  zoom    = 14,
  scale   = 2
)

# ---------------------------------------------
# 5. Build the “big” hex‐map with custom legend
# ---------------------------------------------

Hex.Map.Big <-
  ggmap(map1.background, interpolate = FALSE) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +

  # Hex‐bin layer: fill & alpha by raw counts
  stat_binhex(
    data   = MedGenMapData,
    aes(
      x     = as.numeric(LON),
      y     = as.numeric(LAT),
      fill  = ..count..,
      alpha = ..count..
    ),
    bins = 80
  ) +

  # Color: viridis “magma” on log10 count, with custom limits
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma",
    trans  = "log10",
    name   = "Count of visits per hexagon",
    limits = c(1, 500),             # adjust min/max as needed
    breaks = c(5, 50, 500),
    labels = comma,
    oob    = squish                   # clamp values outside limits
  ) +

  # Alpha: also on log10(count)
  scale_alpha_continuous(
    trans = "log10",
    range = c(0.6, 1),
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  # Legend: title above the bar, centered, overlapping slightly
  guides(
    fill = guide_colorbar(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust    = 0.5,
      barwidth       = unit(5, "cm"),
      barheight      = unit(0.3, "cm")
    )
  ) +

  # Insert the label‐tiles on top of the background
  inset_ggmap(map1.labels) +

  # Theme: float the legend inside bottom‐right
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position      = c(0.97, 0.03),    # x=0.95, y=0.05 in [0,1] panel coords
    legend.justification = c(1, 0),          # anchor top‐right of legend box at that point
    legend.direction     = "horizontal",

    # Semi-transparent white background behind legend
    legend.background    = element_rect(
                             fill  = alpha("white", 0.7),
                             color = NA
                           ),
    legend.margin = margin(2.5, 8, 1, 8),

    # Title on top of the bar (smaller, bold, pulled down slightly)
    legend.title.align   = 0.5,
    legend.title         = element_text(
                             size   = 8,
                             face   = "bold",
                             margin = margin(b = +5)
                           ),

    # Legend labels: smaller, bold
    legend.text          = element_text(
                             size = 6,
                             face = "bold"
                           ),

    # Remove any extra vertical spacing
    legend.spacing.y     = unit(0, "pt")
  )

# ---------------------------------------------
# 6. Build the “small” hex‐map (to inset)
# ---------------------------------------------
Hex.Map.Small <-
  ggmap(map2.background, interpolate = FALSE, darken = 0.05) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +

  stat_binhex(
    data   = MedGenMapData,
    aes(
      x     = as.numeric(LON),
      y     = as.numeric(LAT),
      fill  = ..count..,
      alpha = ..count..
    ),
    bins = 32
  ) +

  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma",
    trans  = "log10",
    name   = NULL,                      # no title on inset
    limits = c(1, 500),
    oob    = squish
  ) +

  scale_alpha_continuous(
    trans = "log10",
    range = c(0.65, 1),
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  # inset_ggmap(map2.labels) +

  theme_void() +

  theme(legend.position = "none")

# ---------------------------------------------
# 7. Add a white border around the small map
# ---------------------------------------------
small_map_framed <-
  Hex.Map.Small +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(
                        color = "white",
                        size  = 2,      # thickness of white border
                        fill  = NA      # transparent fill; use "white" if you want a white box behind
                      ),
    plot.margin     = margin(2, 2, 2, 2),  # padding so border isn't clipped

    # remove axes/text if any remained
    axis.text       = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks      = element_blank(),
    axis.title      = element_blank()
  )

# ---------------------------------------------
# 8. Combine Big + Inset
# ---------------------------------------------
final_plot <-
  Hex.Map.Big +
    inset_element(
      small_map_framed,
      left     = 0,
      bottom   = 0.645,
      right    = 0.4,
      top      = 1,
      align_to = "full"
    )

# 9. Render
print(final_plot)
```

## Statistics: differences between demographic groups {#fig1-stats}

<details class="stats">
<summary>Demographic Differences by Age</summary>

```{r stats-demo-differences-by-age, fig.width=11, fig.height=20, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 1 > Statistics: differences between demographic groups
## What    : Significance of Age Differences by Demographic Group (Kruskal-Wallis Test for All)
## Creates : demo_data, summarize_age_by, tab_gender, tab_race, tab_insurance, tab_visit, age_summary_table
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare demo_data with recoding
demo_data <- MedGenData %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE),
    !is.na(GENDER), GENDER != "X", GENDER != "NA",
    !is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA",
    !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NA",
    !is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    # Insurance class
    INSURANCE_CLASS = dplyr::case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS),
    # Visit type collapsing
    VISIT_TYPE = dplyr::case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    VISIT_TYPE = factor(VISIT_TYPE),
    VISIT_AGE = as.numeric(VISIT_AGE)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_TYPE))

# Summarizing function (for all data, no stratification)
summarize_age_by <- function(data, group_var, group_label) {
  kw <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste("VISIT_AGE ~", group_var)), data = data)
  group_stats <- data %>%
    group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      Mean_Age = round(mean(VISIT_AGE, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      Median_Age = round(median(VISIT_AGE, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  parent_row <- data.frame(
    Variable = group_label,
    Level = "",
    n = "",
    Mean_Age = "",
    Median_Age = "",
    Test = "Kruskal-Wallis",
    p.value = signif(kw$p.value, 3),
    Significant = ifelse(kw$p.value < 0.05, "Yes", "No"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  sub_rows <- data.frame(
    Variable = "",
    Level = paste0("   - ", as.character(group_stats[[group_var]])),
    n = group_stats$n,
    Mean_Age = group_stats$Mean_Age,
    Median_Age = group_stats$Median_Age,
    Test = "",
    p.value = "",
    Significant = "",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  rbind(parent_row, sub_rows)
}

# Use this function for each demographic variable
tab_gender <- summarize_age_by(demo_data, "GENDER", "Gender")
tab_race <- summarize_age_by(demo_data, "RACE", "Race (collapsed)")
tab_insurance <- summarize_age_by(demo_data, "INSURANCE_CLASS", "Insurance Class")
tab_visit <- summarize_age_by(demo_data, "VISIT_TYPE", "Visit Type")

# Bind together
age_summary_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(tab_gender, tab_race, tab_insurance, tab_visit)

# Print
knitr::kable(
  age_summary_table,
  align = "l",
  caption = "Significance of Age Differences by Demographic Group (Kruskal-Wallis Test for All)"
)

<details class="stats">
<summary>Demographic Differences Significant Confounding</summary>

```{r stats-demo-differences-by-race, fig.width=11, fig.height=20, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 1 > Statistics: differences between demographic groups
## What    : Type III Tests: Predictors of Each Demographic Variable (controlling for all others)
## Creates : demo_data, demographics, variable_types, lookup, regression_data, get_pval_col, analyze_demographic, all_results, summary_table
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# collapse_insurance() is defined once in the "helpers" chunk at the top of the notebook.

# Prep data
demo_data <- MedGenData %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA",
    !is.na(GENDER), GENDER %in% c("Female", "Male"),
    !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS),
    !is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = collapse_insurance(FINANCIAL_CLASS),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS),
    VISIT_TYPE = dplyr::case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP == "NEW PATIENT VISIT" ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP == "NPV TELEHEALTH" ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP == "RETURN PATIENT VISIT" ~ "Follow up",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP == "RETURN ANNUAL VISIT" ~ "Follow up",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP == "RPV TELEHEALTH" ~ "Follow up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_TYPE))

# Specify variable types and names
demographics <- c("VISIT_AGE", "GENDER", "VISIT_TYPE", "INDICATION", "RACE", "INSURANCE_CLASS")
variable_types <- c(
  VISIT_AGE = "continuous",
  GENDER = "binary",
  VISIT_TYPE = "binary",
  INDICATION = "categorical",
  RACE = "categorical",
  INSURANCE_CLASS = "categorical"
)

# Make a human-readable lookup for display
lookup <- c(
  VISIT_AGE = "Age",
  GENDER = "Gender",
  VISIT_TYPE = "Visit Type",
  INDICATION = "Indication",
  RACE = "Race",
  INSURANCE_CLASS = "Insurance Class"
)

# Clean data: ensure all predictors are factors except VISIT_AGE
regression_data <- demo_data %>%
  mutate(
    GENDER = factor(GENDER),
    VISIT_TYPE = factor(VISIT_TYPE),
    INDICATION = factor(Indication.Group),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS)
  )

# Function to robustly extract p-value column
get_pval_col <- function(df, possible = c("Pr(>F)", "Pr(>Chi)", "Pr(>Chisq)")) {
  intersect(possible, names(df))[1]
}

# Main analysis function
analyze_demographic <- function(outcome, predictors, variable_types, data) {
  sub_data <- data %>%
    select(all_of(c(outcome, predictors))) %>%
    na.omit()
  predictors_str <- paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")
  formula <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", predictors_str))

  type <- variable_types[[outcome]]
  result <- NULL
  if (type == "continuous") {
    model <- lm(formula, data = sub_data)
    anova_tab <- car::Anova(model, type = 3)
    res <- as.data.frame(anova_tab)
    res$Predictor <- rownames(res)
    res <- res[res$Predictor != "(Intercept)", ]
    pval_col <- get_pval_col(res, "Pr(>F)")
    res <- res %>%
      transmute(
        Outcome = outcome,
        Predictor,
        Test = "F",
        Statistic = round(F, 2),
        p.value = signif(.data[[pval_col]], 3),
        Significant = ifelse(.data[[pval_col]] < 0.05, "Yes", "No")
      )
    result <- res
  } else if (type == "binary") {
    model <- glm(formula, data = sub_data, family = binomial)
    anova_tab <- car::Anova(model, type = 3, test.statistic = "Wald")
    res <- as.data.frame(anova_tab)
    res$Predictor <- rownames(res)
    res <- res[res$Predictor != "(Intercept)", ]
    pval_col <- get_pval_col(res, c("Pr(>Chi)", "Pr(>Chisq)"))
    res <- res %>%
      transmute(
        Outcome = outcome,
        Predictor,
        Test = "Wald Chi-sq",
        Statistic = round(Chisq, 2),
        p.value = signif(.data[[pval_col]], 3),
        Significant = ifelse(.data[[pval_col]] < 0.05, "Yes", "No")
      )
    result <- res
  } else if (type == "categorical") {
    model <- nnet::multinom(formula, data = sub_data, trace = FALSE)
    anova_tab <- car::Anova(model, type = 3)
    res <- as.data.frame(anova_tab)
    res$Predictor <- rownames(res)
    res <- res[res$Predictor != "(Intercept)", ]
    chisq_col <- intersect(c("LR Chisq", "Chisq", "LR.Chisq"), names(res))[1]
    pval_col <- get_pval_col(res, c("Pr(>Chisq)", "Pr(>Chi)"))
    res <- res %>%
      transmute(
        Outcome = outcome,
        Predictor,
        Test = "LR Chi-sq",
        Statistic = round(.data[[chisq_col]], 2),
        p.value = signif(.data[[pval_col]], 3),
        Significant = ifelse(.data[[pval_col]] < 0.05, "Yes", "No")
      )
    result <- res
  }
  result
}

# Loop and stack results
all_results <- list()
for (outcome in demographics) {
  predictors <- setdiff(demographics, outcome)
  res <- analyze_demographic(outcome, predictors, variable_types, regression_data)
  all_results[[outcome]] <- res
}
summary_table <- bind_rows(all_results)

# Make output readable
summary_table <- summary_table %>%
  mutate(
    Outcome = lookup[Outcome],
    Predictor = lookup[Predictor]
  )

# Print stacked table
knitr::kable(
  summary_table,
  caption = "Type III Tests: Predictors of Each Demographic Variable (controlling for all others)",
  align = "l"
)
```
</details>

# <span class="fig-badge">Figure 2</span> Demographic characteristics and visit types across clinical indications {#fig2}

### Shared preparation: 6-month date bins and indication ordering {#fig2-shared-dates}

<div class="note">These statements are used by more than one panel below, so they run once here. Each panel's own chunk then contains the code specific to that panel.</div>

```{r fig2-shared-dates}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Shared preparation]  Figure 2 > Shared preparation: 6-month date bins and indication ordering
## What    : Statements used by more than one panel of this figure; run once here, before the panel chunks.
## Creates : start_all, end_all, breaks_6mo, MedGenData, base_levels, final_levels
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

MedGenData$CONTACT_DATE <- as.Date(MedGenData$CONTACT_DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")

MedGenData$CONTACT_DATE_MONTH <- cut(MedGenData$CONTACT_DATE, breaks='quarter')

MedGenData$CONTACT_DATE_YEAR <- cut(MedGenData$CONTACT_DATE, breaks='year')

# Find the full range, snapped to January 1 and July 1
start_all <- floor_date(min(MedGenData$CONTACT_DATE, na.rm = TRUE), "year")

end_all   <- ceiling_date(max(MedGenData$CONTACT_DATE, na.rm = TRUE), "year")

# Create a sequence of 6-month breaks: Jan 1, Jul 1, Jan 1, Jul 1, …
breaks_6mo <- seq(from = start_all, to = end_all, by = "6 months")

MedGenData <- MedGenData %>%
  mutate(
    half_idx = findInterval(CONTACT_DATE, breaks_6mo, rightmost.closed = FALSE),
    half_idx = ifelse(half_idx == 0, 1, half_idx),
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF = breaks_6mo[half_idx]
  ) %>%
  select(-half_idx)

# 5. (Optional) If you also want a human‐readable label like “Jan 2016” / “Jul 2016”:
MedGenData <- MedGenData %>%
  mutate(
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF_LABEL = format(CONTACT_DATE_HALF, "%b %Y"))

# Plotting order
base_levels <- MedGenData %>%
  count(Indication.Group) %>%
  arrange(n) %>%
  pull(Indication.Group)

# 2) Move “Hypermobility” to the end
final_levels <- c(setdiff(base_levels, "Hypermobility"), "Hypermobility")
```

## 2A · Indications for all visits {#fig2a}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Indications for all 9,867 unique patient visits, October 1, 2016 to September 30, 2024. The percentage of each indication relative to the total is shown in the legend.</div>

```{r fig2a-indications-pie, fig.width=10, fig.height=5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 2 > 2A · Indications for all visits
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : Plot.Indication.Pie
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Plot.Indication.Pie <- MedGenData %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group) %>%
  count(name = "n") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    perc = n / sum(n),
    # Build the raw label text
    labels = paste0(Indication.Group, ", ", round(perc * 100, 2), "%")
  ) %>%
  # Re‐factor Indication.Group to rev(final_levels)
  mutate(
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group, levels = rev(final_levels))
  ) %>%
  # Now turn labels into a factor whose levels follow that same order:
  mutate(
    labels = factor(
      labels,
      levels = paste0(
        rev(final_levels),
        ", ",
        round(
          (n[match(rev(final_levels), Indication.Group)] / sum(n)) * 100,
          2
        ),
        "%"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = "",
    y = perc,
    fill = labels       # <- now fill is the factor “Group, XX.XX%”
  )) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(fill = "Indication, % of total") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = rev(c(stepped2(20), "grey30"))
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1, reverse = TRUE)
  )

# ---- display ----

print(Plot.Indication.Pie + guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)))

Indications with a significant decrease in proportion over time (Hypermobility, Connective tissue disorder) are marked with a blue asterisk; those with a significant increase (Cancer genetics, Multisystem disorder, Lysosomal storage, Chromosomal disorder, Renal disorder, Lung disorder, Gastrointestinal disorder) with a red asterisk. Logistic regression, corrected across all 21 indication groups.</div>

```{r fig2b-indications-over-time, fig.width=12, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 2 > 2B · Indications over time
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : Plot.Indication.Year
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# PLot by half year

  plot_df <- MedGenData %>%
  # 1) Count per half‐year × indication, then turn raw count into a proportion
  group_by(CONTACT_DATE_HALF, Indication.Group) %>%
  count(name = "n") %>%
  group_by(CONTACT_DATE_HALF) %>%
  mutate(n = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  # 2) Re‐factor Indication.Group to your desired final_levels
  mutate(Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group, levels = final_levels)) %>%

  # 3) Spread so that each half‐year becomes its own column (with missing → 0)
  spread(key = CONTACT_DATE_HALF, value = n, fill = 0) %>%

  # 4) Gather back into long form
  gather(key = "CONTACT_DATE_HALF", value = "n", -Indication.Group) %>%

  # 5) Convert CONTACT_DATE_HALF (e.g. "2020-01-01") into Date
  #    If CONTACT_DATE_HALF was originally created via as.Date(…) then this will work:
  mutate(
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF = as.Date(CONTACT_DATE_HALF)
  )

# 6) Plot, adding a custom x-axis that shows "Jan 2020", "Jul 2020", … rather than raw dates
Plot.Indication.Year <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(
    x    = CONTACT_DATE_HALF,
    y    = n,
    fill = Indication.Group
  )) +
  geom_area(color = "grey80") +

  # Y‐axis as percentages, no extra space
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +

  # X‐axis: ticks every six months, labeled "Jan YYYY" / "Jul YYYY"
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "6 months",
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +

  # Axis labels, title, legend
  ylab("Percent of referrals for each indication") +
  xlab("Date (by half-year)") +
  labs(fill = "Referral Indication") +

  # Your color palette in the same Indication.Group order
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = as.vector(c(stepped2(20), "grey30"))
  ) +

  # Minimal theme + rotate x‐labels 90°
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)
  ) +

  # Legend tweaks
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      ncol         = 1,
      override.aes = list(color = "grey80"),
      keywidth     = 0.3,
      keyheight    = 0.3,
      default.unit = "inch"
    )
  )

# ---- display ----

print(Plot.Indication.Year + guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)))

<details class="stats">
<summary>Stats on indications over time</summary>

```{r indications-over-time-stats, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 2 > 2B · Indications over time
## What    : Per-Group Logistic Regression: Change in Odds of Each Indication Over Time
## Creates : ind_data, indication_list, results, all_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare the data
ind_data <- MedGenData %>%
  filter(!is.na(Indication.Group), !is.na(CONTACT_DATE_HALF)) %>%
  filter(Indication.Group != "NA") %>%
  mutate(
    Indication.Group = as.character(Indication.Group),
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF = as.numeric(as.factor(CONTACT_DATE_HALF))
  )

indication_list <- unique(ind_data$Indication.Group)

results <- lapply(indication_list, function(g) {
  dat <- ind_data %>%
    mutate(Y = as.integer(Indication.Group == g))
  fit <- glm(Y ~ CONTACT_DATE_HALF, data = dat, family = binomial())
  tidy_fit <- broom::tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
  out <- tidy_fit %>%
    filter(term == "CONTACT_DATE_HALF") %>%
    mutate(
      `Indication Group` = g,
      OR = estimate,
      OR_low = conf.low,
      OR_high = conf.high,
      `Odds Ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, OR_low, OR_high),
      `p-value` = p.value
    ) %>%
    select(`Indication Group`, `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`, `p-value`)
  return(out)
})

# Combine all
all_results <- bind_rows(results) %>%
  mutate(
    `Adjusted p-value` = p.adjust(`p-value`, method = "bonferroni"),
    Direction = case_when(
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & as.numeric(sub(" .*", "", `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`)) > 1 ~ "Increasing over time",
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & as.numeric(sub(" .*", "", `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`)) < 1 ~ "Decreasing over time",
      TRUE ~ "No difference"
    ),
    `p-value` = formatC(`p-value`, format = "e", digits = 2),
    `Adjusted p-value` = formatC(`Adjusted p-value`, format = "e", digits = 2)
  )

DT::datatable(
  all_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Per-Group Logistic Regression: Change in Odds of Each Indication Over Time",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Statistical Analysis of Patient Age Differences, by Indication</summary>

```{r stats-age-by-indication, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 2 > 2C · Patient age, by indication
## What    : Wilcoxon Test: Age Differences Between Each Indication Group and the Overall Cohort
## Creates : age_test_data, overall_mean_age, wilcox_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare dataset
age_test_data <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_AGE), !is.na(Indication.Group))

# Calculate overall mean age
overall_mean_age <- mean(age_test_data$VISIT_AGE, na.rm = TRUE)

# Perform Wilcoxon test for each group vs. the rest
wilcox_results <- age_test_data %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Age = round(mean(VISIT_AGE), 1),
    Median_Age = round(median(VISIT_AGE), 1),
    p_value_raw = wilcox.test(
      VISIT_AGE,
      age_test_data$VISIT_AGE[!(age_test_data$Indication.Group %in% Indication.Group)],
      alternative = "two.sided"
    )$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p_value_adj = p.adjust(p_value_raw, method = "bonferroni"),
    `p-value` = format.pval(p_value_raw, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE),
    `Adjusted p-value` = format.pval(p_value_adj, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE),
    `Direction of Difference` = case_when(
      p_value_adj < 0.05 & Mean_Age > overall_mean_age ~ "Higher than overall mean",
      p_value_adj < 0.05 & Mean_Age < overall_mean_age ~ "Lower than overall mean",
      TRUE ~ "No Difference"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
    `Mean Age` = Mean_Age,
    `Median Age` = Median_Age,
    `p-value`,
    `Adjusted p-value`,
    `Direction of Difference`
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(`Mean Age`))

# Display as interactive table
DT::datatable(
  wilcox_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Wilcoxon Test: Age Differences Between Each Indication Group and the Overall Cohort",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

</details>

<details class="stats">
<summary>Statistical Analysis of Patient Age Differences, by Indication, with Covariates</summary>

```{r stats-age-by-indication-covariates, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 2 > 2C · Patient age, by indication
## What    : Adjusted Mean Age by Indication Group (linear model, adjusted for Sex, Race, Insurance, and Visit Type)
## Creates : age_test_data, lm_model, emm, emm_df, contrast_vs_overall, contrast_df, overall_mean, final_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load required libraries

# Helper function to collapse insurance categories
# collapse_insurance() is defined once in the "helpers" chunk at the top of the notebook.

# Prepare dataset
age_test_data <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE), !is.na(Indication.Group),
    !is.na(GENDER), !is.na(RACE),
    !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), !is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    GENDER = factor(GENDER),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = collapse_insurance(FINANCIAL_CLASS),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS),
    VISIT_TYPE = dplyr::case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    VISIT_TYPE = factor(VISIT_TYPE),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_TYPE))

# Fit linear model
lm_model <- lm(VISIT_AGE ~ Indication.Group + GENDER + INSURANCE_CLASS + VISIT_TYPE + RACE, data = age_test_data)

# Marginal means for each Indication.Group (with CI)
emm <- emmeans(lm_model, "Indication.Group")
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm) %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Age = emmean,
    Lower_CI = lower.CL,
    Upper_CI = upper.CL,
    row_id = row_number()
  )

# Effect coding contrasts (each group vs. overall mean)
contrast_vs_overall <- contrast(emm, method = "eff", infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
contrast_df <- as.data.frame(contrast_vs_overall) %>%
  mutate(
    pval_raw = p.value,
    pval_adj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni"),
    row_id = row_number()
  )

# Overall mean for direction reference
overall_mean <- mean(age_test_data$VISIT_AGE, na.rm = TRUE)

# Join and calculate direction and beta [CI]
final_results <- emm_df %>%
  left_join(
    contrast_df %>% select(row_id, estimate, lower.CL, upper.CL, pval_raw, pval_adj),
    by = "row_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Direction = case_when(
      pval_adj < 0.05 & Mean_Age > overall_mean ~ "Higher than overall mean",
      pval_adj < 0.05 & Mean_Age < overall_mean ~ "Lower than overall mean",
      TRUE ~ "No Difference"
    ),
    `Mean Age (adj)` = round(Mean_Age, 1),
    `Lower CI` = round(Lower_CI, 1),
    `Upper CI` = round(Upper_CI, 1),
    `p-value` = format.pval(pval_raw, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE),
    `Adjusted p-value` = format.pval(pval_adj, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE),
    `Beta [CI]` = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", estimate, lower.CL.y, upper.CL.y)
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication.Group`,
    `Mean Age (adj)`,
    `Lower CI`,
    `Upper CI`,
    `p-value`,
    `Adjusted p-value`,
    `Beta [CI]`,
    Direction
  )

# Display interactive table
DT::datatable(
  final_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Adjusted Mean Age by Indication Group (linear model, adjusted for Sex, Race, Insurance, and Visit Type)",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Statistical Analysis of Patient Race Differences, by Indication</summary>

```{r stats-race-by-indication, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 2 > 2D · Patient race, by indication
## What    : Chi-square Test of Racial Composition by Indication Group (vs. Rest of Cohort)
## Creates : all_races, race_counts_by_group, total_counts, indication_groups, chi_sq_results, chi_sq_df
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Get all unique races
all_races <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(!is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA") %>%
  pull(RACE) %>% unique() %>% sort()

# Prepare group-race count table
race_counts_by_group <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(!is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA", !is.na(Indication.Group)) %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group, RACE) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(Indication.Group, RACE = all_races, fill = list(n = 0))

# Prepare total counts for the whole cohort
total_counts <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(!is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA", !is.na(Indication.Group)) %>%
  group_by(RACE) %>%
  summarise(n_total = n(), .groups = "drop")

# List of all indication groups
indication_groups <- unique(race_counts_by_group$Indication.Group)

# Run chi-square test for each group vs rest of cohort
chi_sq_results <- lapply(indication_groups, function(group) {
  # Group counts
  grp <- race_counts_by_group %>% filter(Indication.Group == group) %>% arrange(RACE)
  grp_counts <- grp$n

  # Rest of cohort counts
  rest <- race_counts_by_group %>%
    filter(Indication.Group != group) %>%
    group_by(RACE) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(RACE)
  rest_counts <- rest$n

  mat <- rbind(grp_counts, rest_counts)

  # If there are any columns with all zeros, remove for test
  keep_cols <- which(colSums(mat) > 0)
  mat <- mat[, keep_cols, drop=FALSE]

  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(mat))
  data.frame(
    `Indication Group` = group,
    `p-value` = test$p.value,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
})

# Combine results and Bonferroni adjust
chi_sq_df <- bind_rows(chi_sq_results) %>%
  mutate(
    `Adjusted p-value` = p.adjust(`p-value`, method = "bonferroni"),
    `Significant After Correction` = ifelse(`Adjusted p-value` < 0.05, "Yes", "No"),
    `p-value` = format.pval(`p-value`, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE),
    `Adjusted p-value` = format.pval(`Adjusted p-value`, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(`Adjusted p-value`)

# Show table
DT::datatable(
  chi_sq_df,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Chi-square Test of Racial Composition by Indication Group (vs. Rest of Cohort)",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

</details>

```{r save-corrplot-stack, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Build (output hidden)]  Figure 2
## What    : Prepares data and builds plot/table objects that are printed in the panel sections below.
## Creates : sig_groups, n_sig
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Identify significant indication groups by chi-square test
sig_groups <- chi_sq_df %>%
  filter(`Significant After Correction` == "Yes") %>%
  pull(`Indication Group`)

# 2. Generate stacked residual plots
n_sig <- length(sig_groups)
if (n_sig > 0) {
  dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
  png(file.path("figures", "stacked_corrplot.png"), width = 1600, height = 400 * n_sig, res = 160)
  par(mfrow = c(n_sig, 1), mar = c(1, 0, 1, 0))

  # Helper function to wrap long labels
  wrap_label <- function(x, width = 12) {
    sapply(x, function(lab) paste(strwrap(lab, width = width), collapse = "\n"))
  }

  for (group in sig_groups) {
    tryCatch({
      dat <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
        filter(!is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA", !is.na(Indication.Group)) %>%
        mutate(GroupFlag = ifelse(Indication.Group == group, group, "Unknown/Other")) %>%
        count(RACE, GroupFlag) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = GroupFlag, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
        column_to_rownames("RACE") %>%
        as.matrix()

      dat <- dat[rowSums(dat) > 0, ]
      chi <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(dat))
      residual_mat <- t(chi$residuals)

      # Wrap labels for readability
      colnames(residual_mat) <- wrap_label(colnames(residual_mat), width = 12)
      rownames(residual_mat) <- wrap_label(rownames(residual_mat), width = 12)

      # Draw residual heatmap
      corrplot(
        residual_mat,
        is.cor = FALSE,
        col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(200),
        tl.col = "black",
        tl.cex = 0.8,
        cl.cex = 0.8,
        title = "",
        mar = c(1, 0, 1, 0)
      )
    }, error = function(e) {
      message("Error in group: ", group, "\n", conditionMessage(e))
    })
  }

  if (dev.cur() != 1) invisible(dev.off())
}
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Statistical Analysis of Patient Race Differences, by Indication, with Covariates, excluding some races</summary>

```{r stats-race-by-indication-covariates, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 2 > 2D · Patient race, by indication
## What    : Adjusted Probability, Odds Ratio (95% CI), and p-values (raw and adjusted) for Each Race and Indication Group (vs overall mean, covariate-adjusted)
## Creates : race_data, races_to_exclude, race_data_filtered, fit_full, emm, prob_df, emm_logit, cont, cont_df_raw, cont_df, merged_df
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Prepare the data (with all recoding)
race_data <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA",
    !is.na(Indication.Group),
    !is.na(GENDER), !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), !is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP),
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    RACE = factor(RACE, levels = unique(RACE)), # Optionally set White as ref
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = dplyr::case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS),
    VISIT_TYPE = dplyr::case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    VISIT_TYPE = factor(VISIT_TYPE),
    VISIT_AGE = as.numeric(VISIT_AGE)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_TYPE))

# Ensure White is the reference for race
if ("White" %in% levels(race_data$RACE)) {
  race_data$RACE <- relevel(race_data$RACE, ref = "White")
}

#Exclude racial groups with too small counts
races_to_exclude <- c("Asian", "Pacific Island", "American Indian")

race_data_filtered <- race_data %>%
  filter(!RACE %in% races_to_exclude)

# 2. Fit multinomial regression
fit_full <- nnet::multinom(
  RACE ~ Indication.Group + GENDER + INSURANCE_CLASS + VISIT_TYPE + VISIT_AGE,
  data = race_data_filtered,
  trace = FALSE
)

# 3. Get model-adjusted probabilities
emm <- emmeans(fit_full, ~ RACE | Indication.Group, type = "response")
prob_df <- as.data.frame(emm) %>%
  rename(
    `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
    Race = RACE,
    Probability = prob
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Probability (%)` = round(100 * Probability, 1),
    `Lower CI` = round(100 * lower.CL, 1),
    `Upper CI` = round(100 * upper.CL, 1)
  ) %>%
  select(`Indication Group`, Race, `Probability (%)`, `Lower CI`, `Upper CI`)

# 4. Get effect-coded contrasts: OR, CI, p-values (vs overall mean)
emm_logit <- emmeans(fit_full, ~ Indication.Group | RACE, type = "link")
cont <- contrast(emm_logit, method = "eff")

cont_df_raw <- as.data.frame(cont)
# Confirm columns: usually Indication.Group and RACE
if ("Indication.Group" %in% names(cont_df_raw) && "RACE" %in% names(cont_df_raw)) {
  cont_df <- cont_df_raw %>%
    mutate(
      `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
      Race = RACE
    )
} else if ("contrast" %in% names(cont_df_raw) && "RACE" %in% names(cont_df_raw)) {
  cont_df <- cont_df_raw %>%
    mutate(
      `Indication Group` = str_remove(contrast, " effect"),
      Race = RACE
    )
} else {
  stop("Could not find group or race columns in contrast results.")
}

cont_df <- cont_df %>%
  mutate(
    OR = exp(estimate),
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, exp(estimate - 1.96*SE), exp(estimate + 1.96*SE)),
    `p-value` = as.numeric(p.value) # Keep numeric for adjustment
  ) %>%
  select(`Indication Group`, Race, `OR (95% CI)`, `p-value`)

# 5. Merge & adjust p-values (keep numeric until formatting for display)
merged_df <- left_join(prob_df, cont_df, by = c("Indication Group", "Race"))

# Only adjust for rows with non-NA, numeric p-values
# After the left_join, keep all p-values numeric
merged_df <- left_join(prob_df, cont_df, by = c("Indication Group", "Race")) %>%
  mutate(
    `p-value (raw)` = `p-value`,
    `Adjusted p-value (FDR)` = p.adjust(`p-value (raw)`, method = "fdr"),
    `Adjusted p-value (Bonferroni)` = p.adjust(`p-value (raw)`, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication Group`, Race, `Probability (%)`, `Lower CI`, `Upper CI`,
    `OR (95% CI)`, `p-value (raw)`, `Adjusted p-value (FDR)`, `Adjusted p-value (Bonferroni)`
  )

# Now display using DT, with p-values formatted (but underlying data is numeric)
DT::datatable(
  merged_df,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Adjusted Probability, Odds Ratio (95% CI), and p-values (raw and adjusted) for Each Race and Indication Group (vs overall mean, covariate-adjusted)",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
) %>%
  DT::formatSignif(
    columns = c("p-value (raw)", "Adjusted p-value (FDR)", "Adjusted p-value (Bonferroni)"),
    digits = 2
  )
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Statistical Analysis of Patient Sex Differences, by Indication</summary>

```{r stats-sex-by-indication, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 2 > 2E · Patient sex, by indication
## What    : Fisher's Exact Test: Gender Differences by Indication Group vs. Overall Cohort
## Creates : gender_test_data, total_male, total_female, gender_test_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare counts per group
gender_test_data <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(GENDER %in% c("Male", "Female"), !is.na(Indication.Group)) %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group, GENDER) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(Indication.Group, GENDER, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = GENDER, values_from = n) %>%
  mutate(Total = Male + Female)

# Total male and female counts for the whole cohort
total_male <- sum(gender_test_data$Male)
total_female <- sum(gender_test_data$Female)

# Run Fisher's test per group vs. rest of cohort
gender_test_results <- gender_test_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    rest_male = total_male - Male,
    rest_female = total_female - Female,
    p_value_raw = fisher.test(matrix(c(Male, Female, rest_male, rest_female), nrow = 2))$p.value
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    `p-value` = signif(p_value_raw, 3),
    `Adjusted p-value` = signif(p.adjust(p_value_raw, method = "bonferroni"), 3),
    `Direction of Difference` = case_when(
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & Male / Total > total_male / (total_male + total_female) ~ "More Males",
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & Male / Total < total_male / (total_male + total_female) ~ "More Females",
      TRUE ~ "No Difference"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
    `Male (n)` = Male,
    `Female (n)` = Female,
    `p-value`,
    `Adjusted p-value`,
    `Direction of Difference`
  ) %>%
  arrange(`Adjusted p-value`)

# Display results
DT::datatable(
  gender_test_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Fisher's Exact Test: Gender Differences by Indication Group vs. Overall Cohort",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

</details>


<details class="stats">
<summary>Statistical Analysis of Patient Sex Differences, by Indication, with Covariates</summary>

```{r stats-sex-by-indication-covariates, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 2 > 2E · Patient sex, by indication
## What    : Adjusted Probability and Odds Ratio for Male by Indication Group (logistic model, adjusted for Age, Race, Insurance, Visit Type)
## Creates : gender_test_data, glm_gender, emm_prob, emm_logit, contrast_logit, contrast_logit_df, emm_prob_df, overall_male_prop, final_gender_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Helper functions
# collapse_insurance() is defined once in the "helpers" chunk at the top of the notebook.

# Data preparation
gender_test_data <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(GENDER %in% c("Male", "Female"),
         !is.na(Indication.Group),
         !is.na(VISIT_AGE), !is.na(RACE), !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), !is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP)) %>%
  mutate(
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = collapse_insurance(FINANCIAL_CLASS),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS),
    VISIT_TYPE = dplyr::case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    VISIT_TYPE = factor(VISIT_TYPE),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_TYPE))

# Fit logistic regression
glm_gender <- glm(GENDER ~ Indication.Group + VISIT_AGE + RACE + INSURANCE_CLASS + VISIT_TYPE,
                  data = gender_test_data, family = binomial)

# emmeans: response (probability) and link (logit) scales
emm_prob <- emmeans(glm_gender, "Indication.Group", type = "response")
emm_logit <- emmeans(glm_gender, "Indication.Group", type = "link")

# Effect contrasts (group vs. overall), SE only
contrast_logit <- contrast(emm_logit, method = "eff")
contrast_logit_df <- as.data.frame(contrast_logit) %>%
  mutate(
    OR = exp(estimate),
    CI_low = exp(estimate - 1.96 * SE),
    CI_high = exp(estimate + 1.96 * SE),
    pval_raw = p.value,
    pval_adj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni"),
    row_id = row_number()
  )

# Probabilities and their CI from emmeans
emm_prob_df <- as.data.frame(emm_prob) %>%
  mutate(
    `Male (adj %)` = round(100 * prob, 1),
    CI_low_prob = round(100 * asymp.LCL, 1),
    CI_high_prob = round(100 * asymp.UCL, 1),
    row_id = row_number()
  )

# Overall male probability for direction logic
overall_male_prop <- mean(gender_test_data$GENDER == "Male", na.rm = TRUE)

# Merge and output
final_gender_results <- emm_prob_df %>%
  left_join(
    contrast_logit_df %>% select(row_id, OR, CI_low, CI_high, pval_raw, pval_adj), by = "row_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, CI_low, CI_high),
    `Prob (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.1f%% (%.1f–%.1f%%)", `Male (adj %)`, CI_low_prob, CI_high_prob),
    `Direction of Difference` = case_when(
      pval_adj < 0.05 & prob > overall_male_prop ~ "More Males",
      pval_adj < 0.05 & prob < overall_male_prop ~ "More Females",
      TRUE ~ "No Difference"
    ),
    `p-value` = format.pval(pval_raw, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE),
    `Adjusted p-value` = format.pval(pval_adj, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
    `Prob (95% CI)`,
    `OR (95% CI)`,
    `p-value`,
    `Adjusted p-value`,
    `Direction of Difference`
  )

DT::datatable(
  final_gender_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Adjusted Probability and Odds Ratio for Male by Indication Group (logistic model, adjusted for Age, Race, Insurance, Visit Type)",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

</details>

<details class="stats">
<summary>Statistical Analysis of Visit Type, by Indication</summary>

```{r stats-visit-type-by-indication, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 2 > 2F · Visit type, by indication
## What    : Fisher's Exact Test: Visit Type Differences by Indication Group vs. Overall Cohort
## Creates : MedGenData_Visits, visit_type_test_data, total_new, total_followup, visit_type_test_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Collapse visit types
MedGenData_Visits <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  mutate(
    VisitType_Collapsed = case_when(
      VisitType %in% c("Follow up", "Follow up, telehealth") ~ "Follow up",
      VisitType %in% c("New patient visit", "New patient visit, telehealth") ~ "New patient",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Prepare counts per group
visit_type_test_data <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(!is.na(VisitType_Collapsed), !is.na(Indication.Group)) %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group, VisitType_Collapsed) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(Indication.Group, VisitType_Collapsed, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = VisitType_Collapsed, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(Total = `New patient` + `Follow up`)

# Total New and Follow Up counts for the whole cohort
total_new <- sum(visit_type_test_data$`New patient`)
total_followup <- sum(visit_type_test_data$`Follow up`)

# Fisher's test per group vs. rest of cohort
visit_type_test_results <- visit_type_test_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    rest_new = total_new - `New patient`,
    rest_followup = total_followup - `Follow up`,
    p_value_raw = fisher.test(matrix(
      c(`New patient`, `Follow up`, rest_new, rest_followup), nrow = 2
    ))$p.value
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    `p-value` = signif(p_value_raw, 3),
    `Adjusted p-value` = signif(p.adjust(p_value_raw, method = "bonferroni"), 3),
    `Direction of Difference` = case_when(
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & (`New patient` / Total) > (total_new / (total_new + total_followup)) ~ "More New Patient Visits",
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & (`New patient` / Total) < (total_new / (total_new + total_followup)) ~ "More Follow Up Visits",
      TRUE ~ "No Difference"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
    `New Patient (n)` = `New patient`,
    `Follow Up (n)` = `Follow up`,
    `p-value`,
    `Adjusted p-value`,
    `Direction of Difference`
  ) %>%
  arrange(`Adjusted p-value`)

# Display results
DT::datatable(
  visit_type_test_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Fisher's Exact Test: Visit Type Differences by Indication Group vs. Overall Cohort",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

</details>

<details class="stats">
<summary>Statistical Analysis of Visit Type, by Indication, Covariate adjusted</summary>

```{r stats-visit-type-by-indication-adjusted, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 2 > 2F · Visit type, by indication
## What    : Adjusted Probability, Odds Ratio (95% CI), and p-values (raw and adjusted) for Each Visit Type and Indication Group (vs overall mean, covariate-adjusted)
## Creates : visit_data, races_to_exclude, visit_data_filtered, fit_visit, emm, prob_df, emm_logit, cont, cont_df_raw, cont_df, merged_df
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Prepare the data (with all recoding)
visit_data <- MedGenData_Visits %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA",
    !is.na(Indication.Group),
    !is.na(GENDER), !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), !is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP),
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = dplyr::case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS),
    VISIT_TYPE = dplyr::case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    VISIT_TYPE = factor(VISIT_TYPE),
    VISIT_AGE = as.numeric(VISIT_AGE)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_TYPE))

# Optional: Exclude very rare race groups
races_to_exclude <- c("Asian",  "Pacific Island", "American Indian")
visit_data_filtered <- visit_data %>%
  filter(!RACE %in% races_to_exclude) %>%
  mutate(
    RACE = droplevels(RACE)
  )

# Make sure "New" is the reference
visit_data_filtered$VISIT_TYPE <- relevel(visit_data_filtered$VISIT_TYPE, ref = "New")

# 2. Fit multinomial regression: VISIT_TYPE as outcome
fit_visit <- nnet::multinom(
  VISIT_TYPE ~ Indication.Group + GENDER + INSURANCE_CLASS + RACE + VISIT_AGE,
  data = visit_data_filtered,
  trace = FALSE
)

# 3. Get model-adjusted probabilities for each Indication.Group
emm <- emmeans(fit_visit, ~ VISIT_TYPE | Indication.Group, type = "response")
prob_df <- as.data.frame(emm) %>%
  rename(
    `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
    `Visit Type` = VISIT_TYPE,
    Probability = prob
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Probability (%)` = round(100 * Probability, 1),
    `Lower CI` = round(100 * lower.CL, 1),
    `Upper CI` = round(100 * upper.CL, 1)
  ) %>%
  select(`Indication Group`, `Visit Type`, `Probability (%)`, `Lower CI`, `Upper CI`)

# 4. Get effect-coded contrasts (OR, CI, p-values vs overall mean)
emm_logit <- emmeans(fit_visit, ~ Indication.Group | VISIT_TYPE, type = "link")
cont <- contrast(emm_logit, method = "eff")
cont_df_raw <- as.data.frame(cont)
if ("Indication.Group" %in% names(cont_df_raw) && "VISIT_TYPE" %in% names(cont_df_raw)) {
  cont_df <- cont_df_raw %>%
    mutate(
      `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
      `Visit Type` = VISIT_TYPE
    )
} else if ("contrast" %in% names(cont_df_raw) && "VISIT_TYPE" %in% names(cont_df_raw)) {
  cont_df <- cont_df_raw %>%
    mutate(
      `Indication Group` = str_remove(contrast, " effect"),
      `Visit Type` = VISIT_TYPE
    )
} else {
  stop("Could not find group or visit type columns in contrast results.")
}

cont_df <- cont_df %>%
  mutate(
    OR = exp(estimate),
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, exp(estimate - 1.96*SE), exp(estimate + 1.96*SE)),
    `p-value` = as.numeric(p.value)
  ) %>%
  select(`Indication Group`, `Visit Type`, `OR (95% CI)`, `p-value`)

# 5. Merge & adjust p-values (numeric for DT sorting)
merged_df <- left_join(prob_df, cont_df, by = c("Indication Group", "Visit Type")) %>%
  mutate(
    `p-value (raw)` = `p-value`,
    `Adjusted p-value (FDR)` = p.adjust(`p-value (raw)`, method = "fdr"),
    `Adjusted p-value (Bonferroni)` = p.adjust(`p-value (raw)`, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication Group`, `Visit Type`, `Probability (%)`, `Lower CI`, `Upper CI`,
    `OR (95% CI)`, `p-value (raw)`, `Adjusted p-value (FDR)`, `Adjusted p-value (Bonferroni)`
  )

# 6. Show sortable, numeric p-value table in DT
DT::datatable(
  merged_df,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Adjusted Probability, Odds Ratio (95% CI), and p-values (raw and adjusted) for Each Visit Type and Indication Group (vs overall mean, covariate-adjusted)",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
) %>%
  DT::formatSignif(
    columns = c("p-value (raw)", "Adjusted p-value (FDR)", "Adjusted p-value (Bonferroni)"),
    digits = 2
  )
```

</details>

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Shared preparation]  Figure 3 > Shared data preparation for this figure
## What    : Statements used by more than one panel of this figure; run once here, before the panel chunks.

#################### Testing Sent by Age

## 3A · Testing sent, by visit type {#fig3a}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Marimekko plot of the percent of visits with testing sent, by visit type (new patient vs. follow-up). Row height is the share of all visits accounted for by each visit type; column width is the percent with or without testing within each type. The stacked bar at left shows the overall visit-type distribution (new patient purple, follow-up orange).</div>

```{r fig3a-testing-by-visit-type, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 3 > 3A · Testing sent, by visit type
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : visit_heights, visit_widths, testing_props, label_positions, Plot.Sent.VistType
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

##################### Testing Sent By Visit Type

visit_heights <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(!is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP), NEW_FOLLOWUP != "NA") %>%
  mutate(NEW_FOLLOWUP = case_when(
    NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
    NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New Patient Visit",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  group_by(NEW_FOLLOWUP) %>%
  count() %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(perc = n / sum(n))

visit_widths <- tibble::tibble(
  NEW_FOLLOWUP = c("New Patient Visit", "Follow up"),
  width = c(visit_heights[which(visit_heights$NEW_FOLLOWUP=="New Patient Visit"),]$perc, visit_heights[which(visit_heights$NEW_FOLLOWUP=="Follow up"),]$perc)
) %>%
  mutate(
    xmin = lag(cumsum(width), default = 0),
    xmax = xmin + width
  )

testing_props <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent %in% c("Yes", "No")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP), NEW_FOLLOWUP != "NA") %>%
  mutate(NEW_FOLLOWUP = case_when(
    NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
    NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New Patient Visit",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  count(NEW_FOLLOWUP, Testing_Sent) %>%
  group_by(NEW_FOLLOWUP) %>%
  mutate(prop_within = n / sum(n)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Testing_Sent)) %>%
  mutate(
    ymin = lag(cumsum(prop_within), default = 0),
    ymax = ymin + prop_within
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(visit_widths, by = "NEW_FOLLOWUP")

# Calculate midpoints for each bar (used to place labels)
label_positions <- visit_widths %>%
  mutate(y = (xmin + xmax) / 2)

Plot.Sent.VistType <- ggplot(testing_props) +

      ymax = xmax,

  ) +

  theme(

  ) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  geom_rect(

      ymax = xmax,
      xmin = -0.075,
      xmax = -0.025,
      fill = factor(NEW_FOLLOWUP,levels = c("New Patient Visit", "Follow up"))

  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c( "New Patient Visit" = "#9a19f5", "Follow up" = "#eea110")) +

```{r testing-sent-gender-stats, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 3 > 3B · Testing sent at new-patient visits, by sex
## What    : Odds of Genetic Testing Sent by Gender (New Patient Visits)
## Creates : regression_data, model_gender, or_table
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare data for logistic regression: Outcome = Testing Sent (Yes/No), Predictor = GENDER
regression_data <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH"),
    Testing_Sent %in% c("Yes", "No"),
    !is.na(GENDER), GENDER != "X",
    !is.na(Indication.Group),
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE),
    !is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA",
    !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NA"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Testing_Sent_Binary = ifelse(Testing_Sent == "Yes", 1, 0),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    # Insurance collapsing as in your previous code
    INSURANCE_CLASS = dplyr::case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS)
  )

model_gender <- glm(Testing_Sent_Binary ~ GENDER, data = regression_data, family = binomial())

# Tidy results and filter for gender (excluding intercept)
or_table <- broom::tidy(model_gender, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
    `p-value` = formatC(p.value, digits = 2, format = "e")
  ) %>%
  select(Predictor = term, `OR (95% CI)`, `p-value`)

# Show datatable
DT::datatable(
  or_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Odds of Genetic Testing Sent by Gender (New Patient Visits)",
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE)
)
```

<summary>Testing Sent by Sex Stats, Adjusted for Indication and Age, with Covariates</summary>

```{r testing-sent-gender-stats-covariates, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 3 > 3B · Testing sent at new-patient visits, by sex
## What    : Odds of Genetic Testing Sent by Gender (Adjusted for Indication Group, Age, Race, and Insurance Class; New Patient Visits)
## Creates : regression_data, model_gender_adj_all, or_table
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare data
regression_data <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH"),
    Testing_Sent %in% c("Yes", "No"),
    !is.na(GENDER), GENDER != "X",
    !is.na(Indication.Group),
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE),
    !is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA",
    !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NA"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Testing_Sent_Binary = ifelse(Testing_Sent == "Yes", 1, 0),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    # Insurance collapsing as in your previous code
    INSURANCE_CLASS = dplyr::case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS)
  )

# Fit logistic regression model with all covariates
model_gender_adj_all <- glm(
  Testing_Sent_Binary ~ GENDER + Indication.Group + VISIT_AGE + RACE + INSURANCE_CLASS,
  data = regression_data,
  family = binomial()
)

# Tidy results: show only gender coefficients (exclude intercept and other covariate terms)
or_table <- broom::tidy(model_gender_adj_all, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(grepl("^GENDER", term)) %>%
  mutate(
    Predictor = gsub("GENDER", "", term),
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
    `p-value` = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(p.value, digits = 2, format = "e"))
  ) %>%
  select(Predictor, `OR (95% CI)`, `p-value`)

# Show table
DT::datatable(
  or_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Odds of Genetic Testing Sent by Gender (Adjusted for Indication Group, Age, Race, and Insurance Class; New Patient Visits)",
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE)
)
