```{r testing-sent-race-stats, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 3 > 3D · Testing sent at new-patient visits, by race
## What    : Fits the model / runs the test described in the section heading and returns a formatted table.
## Creates : logit_race_data, model, logit_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare data
logit_race_data <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH"),
    Testing_Sent %in% c("Yes", "No"),
    !is.na(GENDER), GENDER != "X",
    !is.na(Indication.Group),
    !is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA",
    !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NA"
  ) %>%
    mutate(
    VISIT_AGE = as.numeric(VISIT_AGE),
    Testing_Sent = ifelse(Testing_Sent == "Yes", 1, 0),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    RACE = relevel(RACE, ref = "White"),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = dplyr::case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS)
  ) %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Testing_Sent, VISIT_AGE, Indication.Group, RACE, GENDER, INSURANCE_CLASS) %>%
  distinct(.keep_all = TRUE)

# Fit logistic regression
model <- glm(Testing_Sent ~ RACE, data = logit_race_data, family = binomial)

# Tidy and format results with Bonferroni-adjusted p-value
logit_results <- broom::tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    `Race (vs White)` = gsub("RACE", "", term),
    `Odds Ratio` = round(estimate, 2),
    `95% CI` = paste0("(", round(conf.low, 2), "–", round(conf.high, 2), ")"),
    `p-value` = formatC(p.value, digits = 2, format = "e")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Bonferroni p-value` = formatC(p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni"), digits = 2, format = "e")
  ) %>%
  select(`Race (vs White)`, `Odds Ratio`, `95% CI`, `p-value`, `Bonferroni p-value`)

# Display as datatable with annotation/caption
DT::datatable(
  logit_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = 'caption-side: top; text-align: left;',
    'Logistic regression results: Odds of having genetic testing sent (Yes vs No) by race, ',
    htmltools::tags$em('restricted to new patient visits. Reference group: White.')
  ),
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE, deferRender = TRUE)
)
```

```{r testing-sent-race-stats-covar, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
  ) %>%
    mutate(
    VISIT_AGE = as.numeric(VISIT_AGE),
    Testing_Sent = ifelse(Testing_Sent == "Yes", 1, 0),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    RACE = relevel(RACE, ref = "White"),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = dplyr::case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS)
  ) %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Testing_Sent, VISIT_AGE, Indication.Group, RACE, GENDER, INSURANCE_CLASS) %>%
  distinct(.keep_all = TRUE)

# Fit logistic regression, fully adjusted
model <- glm(
  Testing_Sent ~ RACE + Indication.Group + GENDER + VISIT_AGE + INSURANCE_CLASS,
  data = logit_race_data,
  family = binomial()
)

# Tidy results for race only (excluding intercept and non-race terms)
logit_results <- broom::tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(grepl("^RACE", term)) %>%
  mutate(
    `Race (vs White)` = gsub("RACE", "", term),
    `Odds Ratio` = round(estimate, 2),
    `95% CI` = paste0("(", round(conf.low, 2), "–", round(conf.high, 2), ")"),
    `p-value` = formatC(p.value, digits = 2, format = "e"),
    `Bonferroni p-value` = formatC(p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni"), digits = 2, format = "e")
  ) %>%
  select(`Race (vs White)`, `Odds Ratio`, `95% CI`, `p-value`, `Bonferroni p-value`)

DT::datatable(
  logit_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = 'caption-side: top; text-align: left;',
    'Logistic regression results: Odds of having genetic testing sent (Yes vs No) by race, ',
    htmltools::tags$em('adjusted for indication group, sex, age, visit type, and insurance class; restricted to new patient visits. Reference group: White.')
  ),
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE, deferRender = TRUE)
)
```

</details>

```{r fig3e-testing-by-indication, fig.width=15, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 3 > 3E · Testing sent at new-patient visits, by indication
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.

################### Testing sent by Indication

  filter(Testing_Sent %in% c("Yes", "No")) %>% filter(NEW_FOLLOWUP =="NEW PATIENT VISIT") %>%

# Testing Sent order
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Testing Sent by Indication Stats, with Covariates</summary>

```{r testing-sent-indications-stats, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 3 > 3E · Testing sent at new-patient visits, by indication
## What    : Adjusted Probability and Odds Ratio for Genetic Testing Sent by Indication Group (logistic model adjusted for Age, Race, Insurance, Gender)
## Creates : testing_data, glm_testing, emm_prob_test, emm_logit_test, contrast_logit_test, contrast_logit_df_test, emm_prob_df_test, overall_test_sent, final_test_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Statistical Analysis of Testing Sent, by Indication, with Covariates

# Helper function
# collapse_insurance() is defined once in the "helpers" chunk at the top of the notebook.

# Data preparation
testing_data <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(
    NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH" ),
    Testing_Sent %in% c("Yes", "No"),
    !is.na(Indication.Group),
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE), !is.na(RACE), !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), !is.na(GENDER)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    TEST_SENT = factor(Testing_Sent, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(collapse_insurance(FINANCIAL_CLASS)),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group)
  )

# Logistic regression
glm_testing <- glm(TEST_SENT ~ Indication.Group + VISIT_AGE + RACE + INSURANCE_CLASS + GENDER,
                   data = testing_data, family = binomial)

# emmeans: probabilities and logits
emm_prob_test <- emmeans(glm_testing, "Indication.Group", type = "response")
emm_logit_test <- emmeans(glm_testing, "Indication.Group", type = "link")

# Effect contrasts (vs. overall mean)
contrast_logit_test <- contrast(emm_logit_test, method = "eff")
contrast_logit_df_test <- as.data.frame(contrast_logit_test) %>%
  mutate(
    OR = exp(estimate),
    CI_low = exp(estimate - 1.96 * SE),
    CI_high = exp(estimate + 1.96 * SE),
    pval_raw = p.value,
    pval_adj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni"),
    row_id = row_number()
  )

# Get predicted probabilities
emm_prob_df_test <- as.data.frame(emm_prob_test) %>%
  mutate(
    `Test Sent (adj %)` = round(100 * prob, 1),
    CI_low_prob = round(100 * asymp.LCL, 1),
    CI_high_prob = round(100 * asymp.UCL, 1),
    row_id = row_number()
  )

# Overall average probability
overall_test_sent <- mean(testing_data$TEST_SENT == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE)

# Merge & annotate results
final_test_results <- emm_prob_df_test %>%
  left_join(
    contrast_logit_df_test %>%
      select(row_id, OR, CI_low, CI_high, pval_raw, pval_adj),
    by = "row_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, CI_low, CI_high),
    `Prob (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.1f%% (%.1f–%.1f%%)", `Test Sent (adj %)`, CI_low_prob, CI_high_prob),

    # Label direction of difference based on OR
    `Direction of Difference` = case_when(
      pval_adj < 0.05 & OR > 1 ~ "Higher Testing Rate",
      pval_adj < 0.05 & OR < 1 ~ "Lower Testing Rate",
      TRUE ~ "No Difference"
    ),

    `p-value` = format.pval(pval_raw, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE),
    `Adjusted p-value` = format.pval(pval_adj, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
    `Prob (95% CI)`,
    `OR (95% CI)`,
    `p-value`,
    `Adjusted p-value`,
    `Direction of Difference`
  )

# Display as datatable
DT::datatable(
  final_test_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Adjusted Probability and Odds Ratio for Genetic Testing Sent by Indication Group (logistic model adjusted for Age, Race, Insurance, Gender)",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

```{r testing-categories-time, fig.width=13.5, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 4 > 4B · Type of testing sent, over time
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : Plot.Test.Quarter, Plot.Test.Half, Plot.Test.Time

### Over Time

#By Quarter
Plot.Test.Quarter <- MedGenData_Indications %>% filter(!is.na(Test.Category) & `Test.Category` != "NA") %>%

# Build the pipeline for half‐year × Lab proportions and plot:
Plot.Test.Half <-
  MedGenData_Indications %>% filter(!is.na(Test.Category) & `Test.Category` != "NA") %>%
    group_by(CONTACT_DATE_HALF, Test.Category) %>%

  # Convert CONTACT_DATE_HALF (character) back into a Date
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Stats on type of testing over time</summary>


```{r testing-type-over-time-stats, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE, results='asis'}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 4 > 4B · Type of testing sent, over time
## What    : Change in Odds of Each Test Category Over Time (Binary Logistic Regression, Bonferroni Adjusted)
## Creates : model_data, test_categories, results, all_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare the data (time as integer)
model_data <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(!is.na(Test.Category), !is.na(CONTACT_DATE_HALF)) %>%
  filter(Test.Category != "NA") %>%
  mutate(
    Test.Category = as.character(Test.Category),
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF = as.numeric(as.factor(CONTACT_DATE_HALF))
  )

# List of unique test categories
test_categories <- sort(unique(model_data$Test.Category))

# For each category, run logistic regression: is this category Y/N as a function of time
results <- lapply(test_categories, function(cat) {
  df <- model_data %>%
    mutate(Y = as.integer(Test.Category == cat))
  fit <- glm(Y ~ CONTACT_DATE_HALF, data = df, family = binomial())
  tidy_fit <- tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
  # Only keep the time term
  tidy_fit %>%
    filter(term == "CONTACT_DATE_HALF") %>%
    mutate(
      `Test Category` = cat,
      OR = estimate,
      OR_low = conf.low,
      OR_high = conf.high,
      `Odds Ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, OR_low, OR_high),
      `p-value` = p.value
    ) %>%
    select(`Test Category`, `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`, `p-value`)
})

# Combine results, adjust p-values, interpret direction
all_results <- bind_rows(results) %>%
  mutate(
    `Adjusted p-value` = p.adjust(`p-value`, method = "bonferroni"),
    `Interpretation` = case_when(
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & as.numeric(sub(" .*", "", `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`)) > 1 ~ "Increasing over time",
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & as.numeric(sub(" .*", "", `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`)) < 1 ~ "Decreasing over time",
      TRUE ~ "No difference"
    ),
    `p-value` = formatC(`p-value`, format = "e", digits = 2),
    `Adjusted p-value` = formatC(`Adjusted p-value`, format = "e", digits = 2)
  )

# Show as datatable
DT::datatable(
  all_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Change in Odds of Each Test Category Over Time (Binary Logistic Regression, Bonferroni Adjusted)",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

</details>


## 4C · Type of testing sent, by indication group {#fig4c}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Type of testing sent, by clinical indication group, for all tests sent during the study period. Each bar shows the proportion of tests of each type within an indication group, color-coded as in the legend "Testing Type, Percent of Total"; the number of tests in each group is shown beneath the axis label. Indication groups are ordered from left to right by decreasing proportion of NGS panels. Statistical comparison of each group's test-type distribution against all other groups combined (unadjusted chi-square, and multinomial logistic regression adjusted for age, EHR-reported sex and race, insurance class and visit type, Bonferroni-corrected across 21 groups) is given in the table below.</div>

```{r fig4c-test-type-by-indication, fig.width=14, fig.height=7, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 4 > 4C · Type of testing sent, by indication group
## What    : Stacked bars of test type within each indication group, ordered by
##           the share of NGS panels; n per group under the axis labels. Uses the
##           same test-type ordering and palette as panel 4A.
## Creates : category_by_indication, indication_levels, test_type_levels, x_labels, Plot.Category.Indication
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

category_by_indication <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    `Test.Category` != "?", !is.na(`Test.Category`), `Test.Category` != "NA",
    !is.na(Indication.Group), Indication.Group != "NA"
  ) %>%
  count(Indication.Group, `Test.Category`, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group) %>%
  mutate(perc = n / sum(n), n_group = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Indication groups ordered by the share of NGS panels (highest first);
# test types ordered by overall frequency, matching the panel 4A palette
indication_levels <- category_by_indication %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group, n_group) %>%
  summarise(ngs_perc = sum(perc[`Test.Category` == "NGS Panel"]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(ngs_perc))

test_type_levels <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes", `Test.Category` != "?", !is.na(`Test.Category`), `Test.Category` != "NA") %>%
  count(`Test.Category`, sort = TRUE) %>%
  pull(`Test.Category`)

category_by_indication <- category_by_indication %>%
  mutate(
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group, levels = indication_levels$Indication.Group),
    `Test.Category`  = factor(`Test.Category`, levels = test_type_levels)
  )

x_labels <- setNames(
  paste0(indication_levels$Indication.Group, "\n(n = ", indication_levels$n_group, ")"),
  indication_levels$Indication.Group
)

Plot.Category.Indication <- category_by_indication %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Indication.Group, y = perc, fill = `Test.Category`)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = x_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Percent of Tests", fill = "Testing Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  ) +
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Test-type distribution by indication group: unadjusted and covariate-adjusted comparison of each group vs. all others</summary>

```{r fig4c-stats, cache=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 4 > 4C · Type of testing sent, by indication group
## What    : Is the test-type distribution for each indication group different from
##           all other groups? Unadjusted chi-square (with Cramér's V) and
##           covariate-adjusted multinomial LRT, Bonferroni-corrected across groups.
##           Cached: the 21 multinomial fits take a few minutes.
## Creates : test_type_data, global_chisq, cramers_v, base_formula, fit_base, test_type_stats
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_type_data <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    `Test.Category` != "?", !is.na(`Test.Category`), `Test.Category` != "NA",
    !is.na(Indication.Group), Indication.Group != "NA",
    !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NULL",
    !is.na(GENDER), GENDER != "X",
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE), !is.na(RACE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Test.Category    = factor(`Test.Category`),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group),
    GENDER           = factor(GENDER),
    RACE             = factor(RACE),
    INSURANCE        = factor(collapse_insurance(FINANCIAL_CLASS)),
    VISIT_TYPE       = factor(if_else(grepl("NEW|NPV", NEW_FOLLOWUP), "New", "Follow-up")),
    # collapse rare test types (< 30 tests) into "Other" for the adjusted model only
    Test.Category.Model = fct_lump_min(Test.Category, min = 30, other_level = "Other")
  )

stopifnot("test_type_data has no rows: check the filters above" = nrow(test_type_data) > 0)

# Global test: does test type depend on indication group at all?
global_chisq <- chisq.test(table(test_type_data$Indication.Group, test_type_data$Test.Category),
                           simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 2000)

cramers_v <- function(tab) {
  chi <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE))$statistic
  sqrt(as.numeric(chi) / (sum(tab) * (min(dim(tab)) - 1)))
}

base_formula <- Test.Category.Model ~ VISIT_AGE + GENDER + RACE + INSURANCE + VISIT_TYPE
fit_base <- nnet::multinom(base_formula, data = test_type_data, trace = FALSE, maxit = 500)

test_type_stats <- map_dfr(levels(test_type_data$Indication.Group), function(g) {
  message("Fitting: ", g)
  d <- test_type_data %>% mutate(is_group = factor(Indication.Group == g, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)))
  tab <- table(d$is_group, d$Test.Category)

  # unadjusted: group vs. rest x test type (Monte Carlo p for sparse cells)
  chi <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 2000))

  # adjusted: LRT for adding the group indicator to the covariate model
  fit_g <- nnet::multinom(update(base_formula, . ~ . + is_group), data = d, trace = FALSE, maxit = 500)
  lrt   <- anova(fit_base, fit_g)
  lrt_p  <- lrt[[grep("Pr", names(lrt))]][2]
  lrt_df <- lrt[[grep("Df",  names(lrt))]][2]

  tibble(
    `Indication Group` = g,
    `Tests (n)`        = sum(d$is_group == TRUE),
    `Chi-square p (unadjusted)` = chi$p.value,
    `Cramér's V`       = cramers_v(tab),
    `LRT p (adjusted)` = lrt_p,
    `LRT df`           = lrt_df
  )
}) %>%
  mutate(
    `Chi-square p (Bonferroni)` = p.adjust(`Chi-square p (unadjusted)`, method = "bonferroni"),
    `LRT p (Bonferroni)`        = p.adjust(`LRT p (adjusted)`, method = "bonferroni"),
    `Different from other groups (adjusted)` = if_else(`LRT p (Bonferroni)` < 0.05, "Yes", "No")
  ) %>%
  arrange(`LRT p (adjusted)`) %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(`Chi-square p (unadjusted)`, `Chi-square p (Bonferroni)`,
             `LRT p (adjusted)`, `LRT p (Bonferroni)`), ~ signif(.x, 3)),
    `Cramér's V` = round(`Cramér's V`, 3)
  )

cat("Global chi-square (indication group x test type): X-squared =",
    round(global_chisq$statistic, 1), ", p =", signif(global_chisq$p.value, 3), "\n")

datatable(
  test_type_stats,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options  = list(pageLength = 25, scrollX = TRUE),
  caption  = "Test-type distribution for each indication group vs. all other groups: unadjusted chi-square with Cramér's V, and multinomial likelihood-ratio test adjusted for age, sex, race, insurance class and visit type (Bonferroni-corrected across 21 groups)"
)
```

</details>

## 4E · Testing laboratories used, over time {#fig4e}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Laboratory choice over time in 6-month intervals. Laboratories significantly increasing in utilization (Ambry) are marked with a red asterisk; those decreasing (UAB, Prevention, Penn, Fulgent, CTGT, ARUP) with a blue asterisk. Vertical lines mark payer, pricing and ordering-infrastructure events described in the Results: Blueprint Genetics introduced a $250 capped-cost policy for self-pay NGS panels in November 2018 and discontinued it in February 2021; Ambry test ordering was integrated into the Penn Medicine EHR in January 2020; Variantyx offered no-cost reflex from any NGS panel to genome sequencing from January 2022 to February 2023; and GeneDx became in-network with Independence Blue Cross in February 2023.</div>

```{r fig4e-labs-over-time, fig.width=13.5, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 4 > 4E · Testing laboratories used, over time
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : lab_levels, Plot.Lab.Half, vlines_df, breaks_6mo
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Define the Lab‐factor ordering:
lab_levels <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    Lab != "?",
    !is.na(Lab),
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    Lab != "NA"
  ) %>%
  distinct(Lab) %>%
  pull(Lab) %>%
  setdiff(c("Ambry", "Invitae", "BluePrint", "GeneDx")) %>%
  c("BluePrint", "GeneDx", "Ambry", "Invitae" )

# Build the pipeline for half‐year × Lab proportions and plot:
Plot.Lab.Half <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  # a) Keep only rows with a valid lab on a sent test
  filter(
    Lab != "?",
    !is.na(Lab),
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    Lab != "NA"
  ) %>%

  # Count by half‐year × Lab, then convert to proportion within each half‐year
  group_by(CONTACT_DATE_HALF, Lab) %>%
  count(name = "n") %>%             # “n” is raw count
  group_by(CONTACT_DATE_HALF) %>%
  mutate(n = n / sum(n)) %>%        # now “n” is fraction of that half‐year
  ungroup() %>%

  # Spread so each half‐year column contains the proportion (missing → 0)
  spread(key = CONTACT_DATE_HALF, value = n, fill = 0) %>%

  # Gather back to long form
  gather(key = "CONTACT_DATE_HALF", value = "n", -Lab) %>%

  # Convert CONTACT_DATE_HALF (character) back into a Date
  mutate(
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF = as.Date(CONTACT_DATE_HALF)
  ) %>%

  # Re‐factor Lab in the desired order
  mutate(
    Lab = factor(Lab, levels = lab_levels)
  ) %>%

  # Plot a stacked‐area chart of proportions over half‐year intervals
ggplot(aes(
    x    = CONTACT_DATE_HALF,
    y    = n,
    fill = Lab
  )) +
  geom_area() +

  # Y‐axis as percentages, no extra padding
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +

  # X‐axis ticks every 6 months, labeled “Jan 2020”, “Jul 2020”, etc.
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = breaks_6mo,
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    expand      = c(0, 0)
  ) +

  # Axis/legend labels
  ylab("Relative use of each testing lab") +
  xlab("Date") +
  labs(fill = "Lab Used") +

  # Custom colors in lab_levels order
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(11, "Spectral"))(32)[1:30],
      rev(colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(7, "Purples"))(11)[5:8])
    )
  ) +

  # Minimal theme + rotate x‐labels 90°
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank()
  ) +

  # Legend as single column with grey outlines
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      ncol         = 1,
      override.aes = list(color = "grey80"),
      keywidth     = 0.25,
      keyheight    = 0.25,
      default.unit = "inch"
    )
  )

# ---- display ----

vlines_df <- data.frame(
  my_dates = as.Date(c(
    "2018-11-01", #BluePrint Begins offering capped cost testing
    "2021-02-01", #BluePrint Stops offering capped cost testing
    "2020-01-01", #Ambry tests become orderable in Epic -- actually probably earlier
    "2022-01-01", #Variantyx offers no cost reflex to genome
    "2023-02-01", #Variantyx stops no cost reflex
    "2023-02-01"  #GeneDx participates with IBC
    )))

# Still need:
#
#
#
#
#
#

breaks_6mo <- sort(unique(MedGenRawData2025$CONTACT_DATE_HALF))

#Map dates to halves
vlines_df <- vlines_df %>%
  mutate(
    half_idx = findInterval(my_dates, breaks_6mo, rightmost.closed = FALSE),
    half_idx = ifelse(half_idx <= 1, 1, half_idx - 1),   # ← subtract 1 safely
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF = breaks_6mo[half_idx]
  ) %>%
  select(-half_idx)

#Jitter duplicates
vlines_df <- vlines_df %>%
  group_by(CONTACT_DATE_HALF) %>%
  mutate(
    jitter_id = row_number(),
    n_dup     = n(),
    # Calculate jitter offset: center around original date
    jitter_days = (jitter_id - (n_dup + 1)/2) * 5  # e.g., ±5 days spacing
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF_JIT = CONTACT_DATE_HALF + jitter_days
  )

print(Plot.Lab.Half +
        geom_vline(
    data = vlines_df,
    aes(xintercept = CONTACT_DATE_HALF_JIT),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color    = c("blue", "blue", "red", "orange", "orange", "green"),
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)))
```

```{r testing-labs-over-time-stats, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 4 > 4E · Testing laboratories used, over time
## What    : Change in Odds of Use for Each Lab Over Time (Binary Logistic Regression, Bonferroni Adjusted)
## Creates : lab_model_data, labs, lab_results, all_lab_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare the data (time as integer)
lab_model_data <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    Lab != "?", !is.na(Lab),
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    Lab != "NA",
    !is.na(CONTACT_DATE_HALF)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Lab = as.character(Lab),
    CONTACT_DATE_HALF = as.numeric(as.factor(CONTACT_DATE_HALF))
  )

# List of unique labs
labs <- sort(unique(lab_model_data$Lab))

# For each lab, run binary logistic regression: is this lab Y/N as a function of time
lab_results <- lapply(labs, function(lab) {
  df <- lab_model_data %>% mutate(Y = as.integer(Lab == lab))
  fit <- glm(Y ~ CONTACT_DATE_HALF, data = df, family = binomial())
  tidy_fit <- tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
  tidy_fit %>%
    filter(term == "CONTACT_DATE_HALF") %>%
    mutate(
      Lab = lab,
      OR = estimate,
      OR_low = conf.low,
      OR_high = conf.high,
      `Odds Ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, OR_low, OR_high),
      `p-value` = p.value
    ) %>%
    select(Lab, `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`, `p-value`)
})

# Combine and adjust
all_lab_results <- bind_rows(lab_results) %>%
  mutate(
    `Adjusted p-value` = p.adjust(`p-value`, method = "bonferroni"),
    `Interpretation` = case_when(
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & as.numeric(sub(" .*", "", `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`)) > 1 ~ "Increasing over time",
      `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & as.numeric(sub(" .*", "", `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`)) < 1 ~ "Decreasing over time",
      TRUE ~ "No difference"
    ),
    `p-value` = formatC(`p-value`, format = "e", digits = 2),
    `Adjusted p-value` = formatC(`Adjusted p-value`, format = "e", digits = 2)
  )

# Display
DT::datatable(
  all_lab_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Change in Odds of Use for Each Lab Over Time (Binary Logistic Regression, Bonferroni Adjusted)",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

```{r stats-insurance-testing-sent, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 4 > Additional analysis: type of testing sent, by insurance class
## What    : Chi-square Test: Insurance Group vs. Test Type
## Creates : insurance_test_full_table, chi_test_full, chi_summary_insurance
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare comprehensive contingency table
insurance_test_full_table <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    !is.na(`Test.Category`),
    `Test.Category` != "NA",
    FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NULL"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    FINANCIAL_CLASS = case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Commercial", "Medicare", "Medicaid", "Self-Pay")) %>%
  count(FINANCIAL_CLASS, `Test.Category`) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = FINANCIAL_CLASS, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Test.Category") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Perform chi-square test
chi_test_full <- chisq.test(insurance_test_full_table)

# Extract test statistics into summary table
chi_summary_insurance <- data.frame(
  Statistic = round(chi_test_full$statistic, 2),
  `Degrees of Freedom` = chi_test_full$parameter,
  `p-value` = formatC(chi_test_full$p.value, digits = 2, format = "e")
)

# Display results with DT
datatable(
  chi_summary_insurance,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Chi-square Test: Insurance Group vs. Test Type",
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE)
)
```
</details>

```{r insurance-testing-sent-bubble-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=4, warning=FALSE}

## What    : Fits the model / runs the test described in the section heading and returns a formatted table.

# Prepare comprehensive contingency table
insurance_test_full_table <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    !is.na(`Test.Category`),
    `Test.Category` != "NA",
    FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NULL"
  ) %>%

      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",

    )
  ) %>%
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Stats for Type of Testing Sent by Insurance, Adjusted for Covariates</summary>

```{r stats-insurance-testing-sent-covariates, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 4 > Additional analysis: type of testing sent, by insurance class
## What    : Odds ratio (95% CI) for each insurance class vs overall mean by test category (only types with ≥100 tests, adjusted for age, sex, race, visit type, and indication group)
## Creates : eligible_tests, insurance_model_data, fit_insurance, emm_ins, cont, cont_df, table_out
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Find eligible test categories
eligible_tests <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes", !is.na(`Test.Category`), `Test.Category` != "NA") %>%
  count(`Test.Category`) %>%
  filter(n >= 100) %>%
  pull(`Test.Category`)

# 2. Prepare data, restrict to those test categories
insurance_model_data <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    !is.na(`Test.Category`), `Test.Category` != "NA",
    `Test.Category` %in% eligible_tests,
    !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NULL",
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE),
    !is.na(GENDER), GENDER != "X", GENDER != "NA",
    !is.na(RACE), RACE != "NA",
    !is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP),
    !is.na(Indication.Group)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    INSURANCE_CLASS = case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS, levels = c("Commercial", "Medicare", "Medicaid", "Self-Pay")),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    VISIT_TYPE = case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    VISIT_TYPE = factor(VISIT_TYPE),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group),
    VISIT_AGE = as.numeric(VISIT_AGE)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(INSURANCE_CLASS), !is.na(VISIT_TYPE), !is.na(RACE))

# 3. Fit multinomial regression
fit_insurance <- nnet::multinom(
  Test.Category ~ INSURANCE_CLASS + VISIT_AGE + GENDER + RACE + VISIT_TYPE + Indication.Group,
  data = insurance_model_data,
  trace = FALSE
)

# 4. Get odds ratios, CI, and p-values for INSURANCE_CLASS × Test.Category
emm_ins <- emmeans(fit_insurance, ~ INSURANCE_CLASS | Test.Category, type = "link")
cont <- contrast(emm_ins, method = "eff")

cont_df <- as.data.frame(cont) %>%
  mutate(
    `Test Category` = if ("Test.Category" %in% names(.)) Test.Category else as.character(str_extract(contrast, "(?<=\\| ).+")),
    `Insurance Class` = if ("INSURANCE_CLASS" %in% names(.)) INSURANCE_CLASS else as.character(str_extract(contrast, "^[^ ]+")),
    OR = exp(estimate),
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, exp(estimate - 1.96*SE), exp(estimate + 1.96*SE)),
    `p-value` = as.numeric(p.value)
  )

# 5. Add Bonferroni adjustment
cont_df <- cont_df %>%
  mutate(
    `Bonferroni p-value` = p.adjust(`p-value`, method = "bonferroni")
  )

# 6. Organize for display
table_out <- cont_df %>%
  select(
    `Test Category`,
    `Insurance Class`,
    `OR (95% CI)`,
    `p-value`,
    `Bonferroni p-value`
  )

# 7. Display table
DT::datatable(
  table_out,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Odds ratio (95% CI) for each insurance class vs overall mean by test category (only types with ≥100 tests, adjusted for age, sex, race, visit type, and indication group)",
  options = list(pageLength = 20, scrollX = TRUE)
) %>%
  DT::formatSignif(columns = c("p-value", "Bonferroni p-value"), digits = 2)
```
</details>

```{r fig4-composite, fig.width=18, fig.height=20}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Plot.Lab.Quarter <- MedGenData_Indications %>% filter(Lab != "?" & !is.na(Lab) & Testing_Sent == "Yes" & Lab != "NA") %>%

    arrange(CONTACT_DATE_MONTH, n) %>% select(-num) %>%
    tidyr::spread(., CONTACT_DATE_MONTH, n, fill = 0 ) %>%

    ggplot(aes(x = as.Date(CONTACT_DATE_MONTH),

			select(Lab) %>% distinct %>%
			filter(!(Lab %in% c("Ambry", "Invitae", "BluePrint", "GeneDx"))) %>% .$Lab), "BluePrint", "GeneDx", "Ambry", "Invitae" )))) +
    geom_area() +

Plot.Lab <- Plot.Lab.Pie  | Plot.Lab.Half

Figure4 <- (
    ((Plot.Category + guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1))) | (Plot.Test.Half + theme(legend.position = "none"))) /
    (Plot.Category.Indication + theme(legend.position = "none")) /
    ((Plot.Lab.Pie + guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1))) | (Plot.Lab.Half + theme(legend.position = "none")))
  ) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect", heights = c(1, 1.1, 1)) +

tryCatch(print(Figure4), error = function(e) cat("Composite could not be rendered in this session:", conditionMessage(e)))
```

# <span class="fig-badge">Figure 5</span> Genetic testing results by patient and test characteristics {#fig5}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> In all panels, bars indicate the percentage of patients with each result classification: pathogenic (blue), VUS (orange), carrier (yellow), candidate gene (aqua; WES/WGS only), or negative (gray). Blue labels give the percent pathogenic. Sample sizes are shown below the axis labels for panels B–F.</div>

## 5A · Results of all genetic testing {#fig5a}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Overall distribution of results for all 4,245 genetic tests sent during the study period.</div>

```{r fig5a-results-overall, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 5 > 5A · Results of all genetic testing
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : plot_data, legend_labels, Testing.Results.Plot
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

###################### Overall Testing Results

# Data prep
plot_data <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  mutate(Classification = ifelse(Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification)) %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Testing_Sent, Result, Classification) %>%
  distinct(.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(desc(Testing_Sent)) %>%
  arrange(PAT_MRN_ID) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, .keep_all = TRUE, ) %>%
  replace(is.na(.), "Negative") %>%
  group_by(Classification) %>%
  count(Classification) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(num = (n)) %>%
  mutate(n = prop.table(n)) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  mutate(
    LABEL = paste0(Classification, " (", round(n*100,digits = 1), "%)")
  )

# Create a named vector for legend labels
legend_labels <- plot_data %>%
  distinct(Classification, LABEL) %>%
  deframe()  # names = Classification, values = formatted label

# Plot
Testing.Results.Plot <- ggplot(data = plot_data,
       aes(
         x = "",
         y = n,
         fill = factor(Classification, levels =
                         rev(c("Negative", "VUS", "Carrier", "Candidate Gene", "Pathogenic"))))) +
  geom_col(position = 'fill') +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  ylab("Result Obtained (Percent)") +
  xlab("") +
  labs(fill = "Testing Result") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Negative" = "grey80",
      "VUS" = "salmon2",
      "Carrier" = "yellow",
      "Candidate Gene" = "cyan3",
      "Pathogenic" = "dodgerblue2"
    ),
    labels = legend_labels  # ✅ updated legend
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  ggtitle("Overall Results") +xlab(NULL)

# ---- display ----

print(Testing.Results.Plot +ggtitle("") + ylab(""))
```

```{r datatable-results-gender, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Interactive table]  Figure 5 > 5B · Results, by sex
## What    : Counts and Percents of Genetic Testing Results by EHR-Reported Sex
## Creates : gender_results_table_long, gender_results_table_wide, col_names, n_cols, pct_cols
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare long-format data
gender_results_table_long <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  mutate(
    Classification = ifelse(is.na(Classification) | Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification)
  ) %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, GENDER, Classification) %>%
  filter(GENDER != "X") %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, GENDER, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  count(GENDER, Classification, name = "n") %>%
  complete(GENDER, Classification, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(GENDER) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Pivot to wide format
gender_results_table_wide <- gender_results_table_long %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = Classification,
    names_from = GENDER,
    values_from = c(n, pct),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) %>%
  rename(`Result Classification` = Classification)

# Get column indices for toggling
col_names <- names(gender_results_table_wide)
n_cols <- which(grepl("^n_", col_names)) - 1
pct_cols <- which(grepl("^pct_", col_names)) - 1

# Create datatable
datatable(
  gender_results_table_wide,
  extensions = "Buttons",
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  options = list(
    dom = 'Bfrtip',
    scrollX = TRUE,
    pageLength = 10,
    buttons = list(
      list(
        extend = "colvisGroup",
        text = "Show Percents",
        show = pct_cols,
        hide = n_cols
      ),
      list(
        extend = "colvisGroup",
        text = "Show Counts",
        show = n_cols,
        hide = pct_cols
      )
    ),
    columnDefs = list(
      list(visible = TRUE, targets = pct_cols),
      list(visible = FALSE, targets = n_cols),
      list(
        targets = pct_cols,
        render = JS(
          "function(data, type, row, meta) {",
          "  return type === 'display' && data !== null ? data + '%' : data;",
          "}"
        )
      )
    )
  ),
  caption = "Counts and Percents of Genetic Testing Results by EHR-Reported Sex"
)
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Stats for Pathogenic Result Probability by Sex</summary>

```{r tresults-gender-stats, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 5 > 5B · Results, by sex
## What    : Odds of Receiving a Pathogenic Result by EHR-Reported Sex (Ref: Female)
## Creates : logistic_data, gender_logit, gender_or_table
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare data for logistic regression
logistic_data <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes", GENDER %in% c("Male", "Female")) %>%
  mutate(
    Classification = ifelse(is.na(Classification) | Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification),
    ResultBinary = ifelse(Classification == "Pathogenic", 1, 0),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male"))  # Female as reference
  ) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, GENDER, ResultBinary, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Fit logistic model
gender_logit <- glm(ResultBinary ~ GENDER, data = logistic_data, family = binomial())

# Format results as ORs
gender_or_table <- tidy(gender_logit, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    `Odds Ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
    `p-value` = signif(p.value, 3)
  ) %>%
  select(`Predictor` = term, `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`, `p-value`)

# Show table
datatable(
  gender_or_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Odds of Receiving a Pathogenic Result by EHR-Reported Sex (Ref: Female)",
  options = list(
    pageLength = 5,
    scrollX = TRUE
  )
)
```

```{r tresults-gender-stats-cov, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),

    VISIT_TYPE = dplyr::case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    VISIT_TYPE = factor(VISIT_TYPE)
  ) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, GENDER, ResultBinary, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_TYPE), !is.na(RACE), !is.na(INSURANCE_CLASS))

# Fit logistic regression: adjusted for all covariates
gender_logit <- glm(
  ResultBinary ~ GENDER + VISIT_AGE + RACE + VISIT_TYPE + INSURANCE_CLASS,
  data = logistic_data,
  family = binomial()
)

# Format results as ORs (show only GENDER coefficients)
gender_or_table <- tidy(gender_logit, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(grepl("^GENDER", term)) %>%
  mutate(
    Predictor = gsub("GENDER", "", term),
    `Odds Ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
    `p-value` = signif(p.value, 3)
  ) %>%
  select(`Predictor`, `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`, `p-value`)

datatable(
  gender_or_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Odds of Receiving a Pathogenic Result by EHR-Reported Sex (Adjusted for age, race, visit type, and insurance class; Ref: Female)",
  options = list(
    pageLength = 5,
    scrollX = TRUE
  )
)
```

## 5C · Results, by age {#fig5c}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Results by age range. p-values from logistic regression of age (continuous), adjusted for sex, race, insurance class, indication group and visit type. Older patients were less likely to receive a pathogenic result and more likely to receive a VUS.</div>

```{r fig5c-results-by-age, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 5 > 5C · Results, by age
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : plot_data, x_axis_labels, label_pathogenic, label_title, Testing.Results.Plot.Age
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

###################### Testing Results by Age

plot_data <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  mutate(AGE_RANGE = cut(VISIT_AGE, breaks = c(0, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 120))) %>%
  mutate(Classification = ifelse(Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification)) %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Testing_Sent, AGE_RANGE, Result, Classification) %>%
  distinct(.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(desc(Testing_Sent)) %>%
  arrange(PAT_MRN_ID) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, AGE_RANGE, .keep_all = TRUE, ) %>%
  replace(is.na(.), "Negative") %>%
  group_by(AGE_RANGE, Classification) %>%
  count(Classification) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(AGE_RANGE) %>%
  mutate(num = (n)) %>%
  mutate(n = prop.table(n)) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  group_by(AGE_RANGE) %>%
  mutate(num=sum(num)) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  mutate(
  AGE_LABEL = case_when(
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(0,25]"    ~ "<25",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(25,35]"   ~ "26–35",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(35,45]"   ~ "36–45",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(45,55]"   ~ "46–55",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(55,65]"   ~ "56–65",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(65,75]"   ~ "66–75",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(75,120]"  ~ ">75",
    TRUE ~ as.character(AGE_RANGE)  # fallback
  ),
  AGE_LABEL = paste0(AGE_LABEL, "\n(n = ", num, ")")
)

# Create x-axis labels
x_axis_labels <- plot_data %>%
  distinct(AGE_RANGE, AGE_LABEL) %>%
  deframe()

# Create label data
label_pathogenic <- plot_data %>%
  filter(Classification == "Pathogenic") %>%
  mutate(
    label = sprintf("%.1f%%", n * 100)
  )

label_title <- label_pathogenic %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  mutate(
    label = "Pathogenic %"
  )

# Plot
Testing.Results.Plot.Age <-  ggplot(data = plot_data,
    aes(
      x = AGE_RANGE,
      y = n,
      fill = factor(Classification, levels =
                      c("Negative", "VUS", "Carrier", "Candidate Gene", "Pathogenic")))) +
  geom_col(position = 'fill') +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  ylab("Result Obtained (Percent)") +
  xlab("Age (years)") +
  labs(fill="Testing Result") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = x_axis_labels) +
  theme(panel.background = element_blank()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values =
                      c("Negative" = "grey80", "VUS" = "salmon2", "Carrier" = "yellow", "Candidate Gene" = "cyan3", "Pathogenic" = "dodgerblue2")) +
  geom_text(
  data = label_pathogenic,
  aes(x = AGE_RANGE, y = 1.025, label = label),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  color = "dodgerblue2",
  size = 3,
) +
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)
  ) +
  ggtitle("Results by Patient Visit Age") +xlab(NULL) +ylab(NULL)

# ---- display ----

print(Testing.Results.Plot.Age + ggtitle(""))
```

```{r datatable-results-age, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Interactive table]  Figure 5 > 5C · Results, by age
## What    : Counts and Percents of Genetic Testing Results by Age Range
## Creates : age_results_table_long, age_results_table_wide, col_names, n_cols, pct_cols
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare long-format summary
age_results_table_long <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  mutate(
    Classification = ifelse(is.na(Classification) | Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification),
    AGE_RANGE = cut(VISIT_AGE, breaks = c(0, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 120))
  ) %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, AGE_RANGE, Classification) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, AGE_RANGE, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  count(AGE_RANGE, Classification, name = "n") %>%
  complete(AGE_RANGE, Classification, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(AGE_RANGE) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
  `Age Range` = case_when(
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(0,25]"    ~ "<25",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(25,35]"   ~ "26–35",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(35,45]"   ~ "36–45",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(45,55]"   ~ "46–55",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(55,65]"   ~ "56–65",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(65,75]"   ~ "66–75",
    as.character(AGE_RANGE) == "(75,120]"  ~ ">75",
    TRUE ~ as.character(AGE_RANGE)  # fallback
  ))

# Pivot wide with separate count and percent columns
age_results_table_wide <- age_results_table_long %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = Classification,
    names_from = `Age Range`,
    values_from = c(n, pct),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) %>%
  rename(`Result Classification` = Classification)

# Identify columns to toggle
col_names <- names(age_results_table_wide)
n_cols <- which(grepl("^n_", col_names)) - 1
pct_cols <- which(grepl("^pct_", col_names)) - 1

# Create interactive datatable
datatable(
  age_results_table_wide,
  extensions = "Buttons",
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  options = list(
    dom = 'Bfrtip',
    scrollX = TRUE,
    pageLength = 10,
    buttons = list(
      list(
        extend = "colvisGroup",
        text = "Show Percents",
        show = pct_cols,
        hide = n_cols
      ),
      list(
        extend = "colvisGroup",
        text = "Show Counts",
        show = n_cols,
        hide = pct_cols
      )
    ),
    columnDefs = list(
      list(visible = TRUE, targets = pct_cols),
      list(visible = FALSE, targets = n_cols),
      list(
        targets = pct_cols,
        render = JS(
          "function(data, type, row, meta) {",
          "  return type === 'display' && data !== null ? data + '%' : data;",
          "}"
        )
      )
    )
  ),
  caption = "Counts and Percents of Genetic Testing Results by Age Range"
)
```

```{r age-results-stats, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 5 > 5C · Results, by age
## What    : Linear Regression Summary: Pathogenic Classification ~ Visit Age
## Creates : model, model_summary, lm_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

model <- lm(
  formula = Classification ~ VISIT_AGE,
  data = MedGenData_Indications %>%
    filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
    mutate(Classification = ifelse(Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification)) %>%
    select(PAT_MRN_ID, Testing_Sent, VISIT_AGE, Classification) %>%
    distinct(.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    arrange(desc(Testing_Sent)) %>%
    arrange(PAT_MRN_ID) %>%
    distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, VISIT_AGE, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      Classification = ifelse(Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification),
      Classification = ifelse(Classification == "Pathogenic", 1, 0),
      Classification = as.numeric(Classification),
      VISIT_AGE = as.numeric(VISIT_AGE)
    ) %>%
    select(VISIT_AGE, Classification)
)

# Get summary
model_summary <- summary(model)$coefficients

# Build results data frame
lm_results <- data.frame(
  Term = rownames(model_summary),
  Beta = round(model_summary[, "Estimate"], 6),
  `Std. Error` = round(model_summary[, "Std. Error"], 6),
  `t value` = round(model_summary[, "t value"], 2),
  `p-value` = formatC(model_summary[, "Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 2, format = "e"),
  check.names = FALSE
) %>%
  filter(Term != "(Intercept)")

datatable(
  lm_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Linear Regression Summary: Pathogenic Classification ~ Visit Age",
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE)
)
```

## 5D · Results, by race {#fig5d}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Results by EHR-reported race. Hispanic or Latino patients of any race were more likely to receive a pathogenic result than White patients; no other differences, by logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, insurance class, indication group and visit type, corrected across 6 groups.</div>

```{r fig5d-results-by-race, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 5 > 5D · Results, by race
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : plot_data, x_axis_labels, plotting_order, label_pathogenic, label_title, Testing.Results.Plot.Race
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

###################### Testing Results by Race

plot_data <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  filter(RACE != "NA") %>%
  mutate(Classification = ifelse(Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification)) %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Testing_Sent, RACE, Result, Classification) %>%
  distinct(.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(desc(Testing_Sent)) %>%
  arrange(PAT_MRN_ID) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, RACE, .keep_all = TRUE, ) %>%
  replace(is.na(.), "Negative") %>%
  group_by(RACE, Classification) %>%
  count(Classification) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(RACE) %>%
  mutate(num = (n)) %>%
  mutate(n = prop.table(n)) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  group_by(RACE) %>%
  mutate(num=sum(num)) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  mutate(
    RACE_LABEL = paste0(RACE, "\n(n = ", num, ")")
  )

# Create x-axis labels
x_axis_labels <- plot_data %>%
  distinct(RACE, RACE_LABEL) %>%
  deframe()

# Testing Sent order
plotting_order <- c(plot_data %>%
  filter(Classification == "Pathogenic") %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  pull(RACE), "Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander")

# Create label data
label_pathogenic <- plot_data %>%
  filter(Classification == "Pathogenic") %>%
  mutate(
    label = sprintf("%.1f%%", n * 100)
  )

label_title <- label_pathogenic %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  mutate(
    label = "Pathogenic %"
  )

# Plot
Testing.Results.Plot.Race <-  ggplot(data = plot_data %>% mutate(RACE = factor(RACE, levels = plotting_order)),
    aes(
      x = RACE,
      y = n,
      fill = factor(Classification, levels =
                      c("Negative", "VUS", "Carrier", "Candidate Gene", "Pathogenic")))) +
  geom_col(position = 'fill') +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  ylab("Result Obtained (Percent)") +
  xlab("EHR-Reported Race") +
  labs(fill="Testing Result") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = x_axis_labels) +
  theme(panel.background = element_blank()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values =
                      c("Negative" = "grey80", "VUS" = "salmon2", "Carrier" = "yellow", "Candidate Gene" = "cyan3", "Pathogenic" = "dodgerblue2")) +
  geom_text(

  aes(x = RACE, y = 1.025, label = label),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  color = "dodgerblue2",
  size = 3,
)  +
  theme_bw()  +
    theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)
  ) +
  ggtitle("Results by EHR-Reported Race") +xlab(NULL)

# ---- display ----

print(Testing.Results.Plot.Race + ggtitle(""))
```

```{r datatable-results-race, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Interactive table]  Figure 5 > 5D · Results, by race
## What    : Counts and Percents of Genetic Testing Results by EHR-Reported Race
## Creates : race_results_table_long, race_results_table_wide, col_names, n_cols, pct_cols
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare long-format summary
race_results_table_long <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  mutate(
    Classification = ifelse(is.na(Classification) | Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification)
  ) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, RACE, Classification, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  count(RACE, Classification, name = "n") %>%
  complete(RACE, Classification, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(RACE) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Pivot to wide format
race_results_table_wide <- race_results_table_long %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = Classification,
    names_from = RACE,
    values_from = c(n, pct),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) %>%
  rename(`Result Classification` = Classification)

# Index columns
col_names <- names(race_results_table_wide)
n_cols <- which(grepl("^n_", col_names)) - 1
pct_cols <- which(grepl("^pct_", col_names)) - 1

# Display with toggle buttons
datatable(
  race_results_table_wide,
  extensions = "Buttons",
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  options = list(
    dom = 'Bfrtip',
    scrollX = TRUE,
    pageLength = 10,
    buttons = list(
      list(
        extend = "colvisGroup",
        text = "Show Percents",
        show = pct_cols,
        hide = n_cols
      ),
      list(
        extend = "colvisGroup",
        text = "Show Counts",
        show = n_cols,
        hide = pct_cols
      )
    ),
    columnDefs = list(
      list(visible = TRUE, targets = pct_cols),
      list(visible = FALSE, targets = n_cols),
      list(
        targets = pct_cols,
        render = JS(
          "function(data, type, row, meta) {",
          "  return type === 'display' && data !== null ? data + '%' : data;",
          "}"
        )
      )
    )
  ),
  caption = "Counts and Percents of Genetic Testing Results by EHR-Reported Race"
)
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Positive by Race Stats</summary>

```{r race-results-stats-path, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 5 > 5D · Results, by race
## What    : Odds of Receiving a Pathogenic Result by EHR-Reported Race (Ref: White)
## Creates : logistic_data_path_race, race_logit_path, race_or_table_path
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare data for logistic regression of pathogenic results by race
logistic_data_path_race <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  mutate(
    Classification = ifelse(is.na(Classification) | Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification)
  ) %>%
  filter(!RACE %in% c("NA")) %>%
  mutate(
    ResultBinary = ifelse(Classification == "Pathogenic", 1, 0),
    RACE = factor(RACE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(RACE = relevel(RACE, ref = "White")) %>%  # Set White as the reference group
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, RACE, ResultBinary, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Fit logistic regression model
race_logit_path <- glm(ResultBinary ~ RACE, data = logistic_data_path_race, family = binomial())

# Format results as Odds Ratios with 95% CI and Bonferroni-adjusted p-value
race_or_table_path <- broom::tidy(race_logit_path, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    `Race Compared to White` = gsub("RACE", "", term),
    `Odds Ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
    `p-value` = formatC(p.value, digits = 2, format = "e")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Bonferroni p-value` = formatC(p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni"), digits = 2, format = "e")
  ) %>%
  select(`Race Compared to White`, `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`, `p-value`, `Bonferroni p-value`)

# Display as datatable
DT::datatable(
  race_or_table_path,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Odds of Receiving a Pathogenic Result by EHR-Reported Race (Ref: White)",
  options = list(
    pageLength = 10,
    scrollX = TRUE
  )
)
```

<details class="stats">
<summary>Positive by Race Stats, Adjusted for Covariates</summary>

```{r race-results-stats-path-cov, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 5 > 5D · Results, by race
## What    : Odds of Receiving a Pathogenic Result by EHR-Reported Race (Adjusted for age, sex, indication, visit type, and insurance class; Ref: White)
## Creates : logistic_data_path_race, race_logit_path, race_or_table_path
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

logistic_data_path_race <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    !is.na(RACE), !RACE %in% c("NA"),
    !is.na(Classification),
    !is.na(GENDER), GENDER %in% c("Male", "Female"),
    !is.na(Indication.Group),
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE),
    !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NA",
    !is.na(NEW_FOLLOWUP)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    RACE = relevel(RACE, ref = "White"),
    Classification = ifelse(is.na(Classification) | Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification),
    ResultBinary = ifelse(Classification == "Pathogenic", 1, 0),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group),
    VISIT_AGE = as.numeric(VISIT_AGE),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = dplyr::case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS == "Self-Pay" ~ "Self-Pay",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(INSURANCE_CLASS),
    VISIT_TYPE = dplyr::case_when(
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "New",
      NEW_FOLLOWUP %in% c("RETURN PATIENT VISIT", "RETURN ANNUAL VISIT", "RPV TELEHEALTH") ~ "Follow up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    VISIT_TYPE = factor(VISIT_TYPE)
  ) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, RACE, ResultBinary, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_TYPE), !is.na(INSURANCE_CLASS), !is.na(Indication.Group))

# Fit logistic regression (adjusted for all covariates)
race_logit_path <- glm(
  ResultBinary ~ RACE + GENDER + Indication.Group + VISIT_AGE + INSURANCE_CLASS + VISIT_TYPE,
  data = logistic_data_path_race,
  family = binomial()
)

# Format results (compare each race to White)
race_or_table_path <- broom::tidy(race_logit_path, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(grepl("^RACE", term)) %>%
  mutate(
    `Race Compared to White` = gsub("RACE", "", term),
    `Odds Ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
    `p-value` = as.numeric(p.value),
    `Bonferroni p-value` = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  select(`Race Compared to White`, `Odds Ratio (95% CI)`, `p-value`, `Bonferroni p-value`)

DT::datatable(
  race_or_table_path,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Odds of Receiving a Pathogenic Result by EHR-Reported Race (Adjusted for age, sex, indication, visit type, and insurance class; Ref: White)",
  options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)
) %>%
  DT::formatSignif(columns = c("p-value", "Bonferroni p-value"), digits = 2)
```
</details>

## 5E · Results, by test type {#fig5e}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Results by type of testing, ordered by likelihood of a pathogenic result. No formal statistical comparisons were performed for this panel.</div>

```{r fig5e-results-by-test-type, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 5 > 5E · Results, by test type
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : plot_data, x_axis_labels, plotting_order, label_pathogenic, Testing.Results.Plot.TestCategory
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

########### Results by type of testing

plot_data <- MedGenRawData2025 %>% filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  filter(
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    !is.na(Test.Category),
    Test.Category != "NA"
  ) %>%
  filter(Test.Category != "RNA Sequencing") %>%
  mutate(Classification = ifelse(Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification)) %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Testing_Sent, Test.Category, Result, Classification) %>%
  distinct(.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(desc(Testing_Sent)) %>%
  arrange(PAT_MRN_ID) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, Test.Category, .keep_all = TRUE, ) %>%
  replace(is.na(.), "Negative") %>%
  group_by(Test.Category, Classification) %>%
  count(Classification) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(Test.Category) %>%
  mutate(num = (n)) %>%
  mutate(n = prop.table(n)) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  group_by(Test.Category) %>%
  mutate(num=sum(num)) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  mutate(
   Test.Category_LABEL = paste0(Test.Category, "\n(n = ", num, ")")
  )

# Create x-axis labels
x_axis_labels <- plot_data %>%
  distinct(Test.Category, Test.Category_LABEL) %>%
  deframe()

# Testing Sent order
plotting_order <- c(plot_data %>%
    filter(Classification == "Pathogenic") %>%
    arrange(desc(n)) %>%
    pull(Test.Category), "RNA Seuencing")

# Create label data
label_pathogenic <- plot_data %>%
  filter(Classification == "Pathogenic") %>%
  mutate(
    label = sprintf("%.1f%%", n * 100)
  )

# Plot
Testing.Results.Plot.TestCategory <-  ggplot(data = plot_data %>% mutate(Test.Category = factor(Test.Category, levels = plotting_order)),
    aes(
      x = Test.Category,
      y = n,
      fill = factor(Classification, levels =
                      c("Negative", "VUS", "Carrier", "Candidate Gene", "Pathogenic")))) +
  geom_col(position = 'fill') +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  ylab("Result Obtained (Percent)") +
  xlab("Test Category") +
  labs(fill="Testing Result") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = x_axis_labels) +
  theme(panel.background = element_blank()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values =
                      c("Negative" = "grey80", "VUS" = "salmon2", "Carrier" = "yellow", "Candidate Gene" = "cyan3", "Pathogenic" = "dodgerblue2")) +
  geom_text(
  data = label_pathogenic,
  aes(x = Test.Category, y = 1.025, label = label),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  color = "dodgerblue2",
  size = 3,
)  +
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)
  ) +
  ggtitle("Results by Testing Category") +xlab(NULL) +ylab(NULL)

# ---- display ----

print(Testing.Results.Plot.TestCategory + ggtitle(""))
```

```{r datatable-results-indication, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## Creates : indication_results_long, indication_results_wide, col_names, n_cols, pct_cols
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare long-format data
indication_results_long <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes", Indication.Group != "NA") %>%
  mutate(
    Classification = ifelse(is.na(Classification) | Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification)
  ) %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Indication.Group, Classification) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, Indication.Group, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  count(Indication.Group, Classification, name = "n") %>%
  complete(Indication.Group, Classification, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Pivot wide: rows = Indication Group, columns = classification types
indication_results_wide <- indication_results_long %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = Indication.Group,
    names_from = Classification,
    values_from = c(n, pct),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) %>%
  rename(`Visit Indication Group` = Indication.Group)

# JS column indices
col_names <- names(indication_results_wide)
n_cols <- which(grepl("^n_", col_names)) - 1
pct_cols <- which(grepl("^pct_", col_names)) - 1

# Render datatable
datatable(
  indication_results_wide,
  extensions = "Buttons",
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  options = list(
    dom = 'Bfrtip',
    scrollX = TRUE,
    pageLength = 10,
    buttons = list(
      list(
        extend = "colvisGroup",
        text = "Show Percents",
        show = pct_cols,
        hide = n_cols
      ),
      list(
        extend = "colvisGroup",
        text = "Show Counts",
        show = n_cols,
        hide = pct_cols
      )
    ),
    columnDefs = list(
      list(visible = TRUE, targets = pct_cols),
      list(visible = FALSE, targets = n_cols),
      list(
        targets = pct_cols,
        render = JS(
          "function(data, type, row, meta) {",
          "  return type === 'display' && data !== null ? data + '%' : data;",
          "}"
        )
      )
    )
  ),
  caption = "Summary of Genetic Testing Results by Visit Indication Group"
)
```

```{r indications-results-stats-path, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 5 > 5F · Results, by indication
## What    : Adjusted Probability and Odds Ratio for Pathogenic Result by Indication Group (logistic model adjusted for Age, Race, Gender, Insurance)
## Creates : path_result_data, glm_path, emm_prob_path, emm_logit_path, contrast_logit_path, contrast_logit_df_path, emm_prob_df_path, overall_path_rate, final_path_results
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Statistical Analysis of Pathogenic Results by Indication Group (adjusted)

# Helper function reused
# collapse_insurance() is defined once in the "helpers" chunk at the top of the notebook.

# Data preparation
path_result_data <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
  filter(
    Testing_Sent == "Yes",
    !is.na(Indication.Group),
    !is.na(VISIT_AGE), !is.na(RACE), !is.na(GENDER), !is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Classification = ifelse(is.na(Classification) | Classification == "NA", "Negative", Classification),
    ResultBinary = ifelse(Classification == "Pathogenic", "Pathogenic", "Other"),
    ResultBinary = factor(ResultBinary, levels = c("Other", "Pathogenic")),
    RACE = factor(RACE),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    INSURANCE_CLASS = factor(collapse_insurance(FINANCIAL_CLASS)),
    Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group)
  )

# Fit logistic regression model
glm_path <- glm(ResultBinary ~ Indication.Group + VISIT_AGE + RACE + GENDER + INSURANCE_CLASS,
                data = path_result_data, family = binomial)

# Estimated marginal means and contrasts
emm_prob_path <- emmeans(glm_path, "Indication.Group", type = "response")
emm_logit_path <- emmeans(glm_path, "Indication.Group", type = "link")
contrast_logit_path <- contrast(emm_logit_path, method = "eff")

# Contrast output: ORs, CI, p-values
contrast_logit_df_path <- as.data.frame(contrast_logit_path) %>%
  mutate(
    OR = exp(estimate),
    CI_low = exp(estimate - 1.96 * SE),
    CI_high = exp(estimate + 1.96 * SE),
    pval_raw = p.value,
    pval_adj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni"),
    row_id = row_number()
  )

# Marginal probabilities (adjusted % pathogenic)
emm_prob_df_path <- as.data.frame(emm_prob_path) %>%
  mutate(
    `Pathogenic (adj %)` = round(100 * prob, 1),
    CI_low_prob = round(100 * asymp.LCL, 1),
    CI_high_prob = round(100 * asymp.UCL, 1),
    row_id = row_number()
  )

# Overall pathogenic rate
overall_path_rate <- mean(path_result_data$ResultBinary == "Pathogenic", na.rm = TRUE)

# Merge and build final output
final_path_results <- emm_prob_df_path %>%
  left_join(
    contrast_logit_df_path %>% select(row_id, OR, CI_low, CI_high, pval_raw, pval_adj),
    by = "row_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, CI_low, CI_high),
    `Prob (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.1f%% (%.1f–%.1f%%)", `Pathogenic (adj %)`, CI_low_prob, CI_high_prob),
    `Direction of Difference` = case_when(
      pval_adj < 0.05 & OR > 1 ~ "Higher Pathogenic Rate",
      pval_adj < 0.05 & OR < 1 ~ "Lower Pathogenic Rate",
      TRUE ~ "No Difference"
    ),
    `p-value` = format.pval(pval_raw, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE),
    `Adjusted p-value` = format.pval(pval_adj, digits = 2, eps = .0001, scientific = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
    `Prob (95% CI)`,
    `OR (95% CI)`,
    `p-value`,
    `Adjusted p-value`,
    `Direction of Difference`
  )

# Show results in interactive datatable
DT::datatable(
  final_path_results,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Adjusted Probability and Odds Ratio for Pathogenic Result by Indication Group (logistic model adjusted for Age, Race, Gender, Insurance)",
  options = list(pageLength = 21, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

```{r indication, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Figure 5 > Additional analysis: pathogenic and VUS results only, by indication
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : Percent.VUS, Percent_Positive_Group, Table2, Result.By.Indication
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Percent.VUS <- MedGenData_Indications %>% filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Indication.Group, Testing_Sent, Result, Classification) %>%
  distinct(.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(desc(Testing_Sent)) %>%
  arrange(PAT_MRN_ID) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, Indication.Group, .keep_all = TRUE, ) %>%
  mutate(Classification = ifelse( (Classification != "VUS" | is.na(Classification)), "None", "VUS")) %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group) %>%
  count(Classification) %>%
  mutate(sum = sum(n[!is.na(Classification)])) %>%
  mutate('Percent VUS' = ifelse(Classification == "None", as.numeric((1-(n/sum))*100), as.numeric(n/sum*100))) %>% ungroup()  %>%
  select(-c(Classification, n)) %>%
  mutate(Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group), sum = round(sum,3),`Percent VUS` = round(`Percent VUS`, 3)) %>% distinct()  %>%
  `colnames<-`(c("Indication.Group", "Number Tested", "Percent VUS"))

Percent_Positive_Group <- MedGenData_Indications %>% filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Indication.Group, Testing_Sent, Result, Classification) %>%
  distinct(.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(desc(Testing_Sent)) %>%
  arrange(PAT_MRN_ID) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, Indication.Group, .keep_all = TRUE, ) %>%
  mutate(Classification = ifelse( (Classification != "Pathogenic" | is.na(Classification)), "None", "Pathogenic")) %>%
  group_by(Indication.Group) %>%
  count(Classification) %>%
  mutate(sum = sum(n[!is.na(Classification)])) %>%
  mutate('Percent Pathogenic' = ifelse(Classification == "None", as.numeric((1-(n/sum))*100), as.numeric(n/sum*100))) %>% ungroup()  %>%
  select(-c(Classification, n)) %>%
  mutate(Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group), sum = round(sum,3),`Percent Pathogenic` = round(`Percent Pathogenic`, 3)) %>% distinct()  %>%
  `colnames<-`(c("Indication.Group", "Number Tested", "Percent Pathogenic"))

Table2 <- left_join(Percent.VUS, Percent_Positive_Group, by = "Indication.Group")

Result.By.Indication <- Table2 %>%
  mutate(
    Indication.Group = str_replace_all(Indication.Group, ' ', '\n'),

print(Result.By.Indication)
```

<summary>Probability of VUS vs Pathogenic per Indication</summary>

```{r vus-path-indication-stats, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Figure 5 > Additional analysis: pathogenic and VUS results only, by indication
## What    : Comparison of VUS vs. Pathogenic Rates by Indication Group (Bonferroni adjusted)
## Creates : vus_path_counts, vus_vs_path_tests
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare counts
vus_path_counts <- MedGenData_Indications %>%
  filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>%
  select(PAT_MRN_ID, Indication.Group, Classification) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, Indication.Group, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Classification = case_when(
    Classification == "VUS" ~ "VUS",
    Classification == "Pathogenic" ~ "Pathogenic",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )) %>%
  count(Indication.Group, Classification) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Classification, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(Total = VUS + Pathogenic + Other)

# Run two-proportion tests
vus_vs_path_tests <- vus_path_counts %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    p_val_raw = tryCatch({
      prop.test(
        x = c(VUS, Pathogenic),
        n = c(Total, Total),
        alternative = "two.sided"
      )$p.value
    }, error = function(e) NA_real_),
    `VUS (%)` = round(100 * VUS / Total, 1),
    `Pathogenic (%)` = round(100 * Pathogenic / Total, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Bonferroni adjustment
vus_vs_path_tests <- vus_vs_path_tests %>%
  mutate(
    `p-value` = p_val_raw,
    `Adjusted p-value` = p.adjust(`p-value`, method = "bonferroni"),
    `p-value (sci)` = formatC(`p-value`, format = "e", digits = 2),
    `Adjusted p-value (sci)` = formatC(`Adjusted p-value`, format = "e", digits = 2),
    Conclusion = case_when(
      !is.na(`Adjusted p-value`) & `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & VUS > Pathogenic ~ "VUS > Pathogenic (adj p < 0.05)",
      !is.na(`Adjusted p-value`) & `Adjusted p-value` < 0.05 & VUS < Pathogenic ~ "Pathogenic > VUS (adj p < 0.05)",
      TRUE ~ "NS"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Indication Group` = Indication.Group,
    `N Tested` = Total,
    `VUS (%)`,
    `Pathogenic (%)`,
    `p-value (sci)`,
    `Adjusted p-value (sci)`,
    Conclusion
  )

# Display as DataTable
DT::datatable(
  vus_vs_path_tests,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Comparison of VUS vs. Pathogenic Rates by Indication Group (Bonferroni adjusted)",
  options = list(pageLength = 25, scrollX = TRUE)
)
```

```{r fig5-composite, fig.width=14, fig.height=15}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```{r circulos-genes, fig.width=30, fig.height=30, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  "Lysosomal storage disorder",
  "Chromosomal disorder"
)

# MedGenData_Indications is built once in the data chunk (see top of notebook).

MedGenData_Indications %>% filter(!is.na(Gene)) %>%
    select(Gene, Classification, Indication.Group) %>%
    filter(Classification == "Pathogenic" | Classification == "VUS") %>%
    #filter(., !grepl("hrom",Gene)) %>%
    #filter(., !grepl("trans",Gene)) %>%
    #filter(., !grepl("arr",Gene)) %>%
    #filter(., !grepl("tris",Gene)) %>%
```
