## Figure S3 · Age distributions of new-patient visits and testing results, by indication group {#figS3}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Panels A–U show all 21 indication groups, ordered by decreasing number of new-patient visits. Above the baseline: stacked kernel-density estimates of age at new-patient evaluation, colored by specific indication (indications representing >5% of the group are labeled; the rest are pooled as "All other indications"). Below the baseline: mirrored densities for the tested subset, colored by result classification (pathogenic/likely pathogenic blue, VUS salmon, carrier yellow, candidate gene cyan, negative gray). Upper density has area 1; lower density has area equal to the proportion tested. Subtitles give new visits, number tested and percent tested.</div>

<div class="note">This chunk is self-contained (it reads <code>MedGenRawData2025</code> directly). The optional <code>ggsave()</code> export to the Desktop is commented out so that knitting does not write files outside the project; uncomment it when you want the PDF.</div>

<div class="zoomable">

```{r new-figure-age-density, fig.width=20, fig.height=29, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Supplement > Figure S3 · Age distributions of new-patient visits and testing results, by indication group
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : All_Indication_Age_Mirrored
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

All_Indication_Age_Mirrored <- local({

  # Settings ---------------------------------------------------------------
  bandwidth_years <- 5
  label_threshold <- 0.05
  legend_font_size <- 7.5
  legend_y <- 1.15  # Slightly higher than the previous position of 0.98

  result_colors <- c(
    "Negative" = "grey80", "VUS" = "salmon2", "Carrier" = "yellow",
    "Candidate Gene" = "cyan3", "Pathogenic" = "dodgerblue2"
  )
  result_order <- c("Pathogenic", "VUS", "Carrier", "Candidate Gene", "Negative")
  result_labels <- c(
    "Pathogenic" = "Pathogenic / likely pathogenic", "VUS" = "VUS",
    "Carrier" = "Carrier", "Candidate Gene" = "Candidate gene", "Negative" = "Negative"
  )
  fmt_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

  # Keep all indication groups, including any with zero new visits.
  all_visits <- MedGenRawData2025 %>%
    transmute(
      Group = trimws(as.character(Indication.Group)),
      Indication = trimws(as.character(Indication_Cleaned)),
      Age = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(VISIT_AGE))),
      Visit = trimws(as.character(NEW_FOLLOWUP)),
      Tested = trimws(as.character(Testing_Sent)) %in% "Yes",
      Outcome = trimws(as.character(Classification))
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Group), !Group %in% c("", "NA", "?"))

  group_levels <- sort(unique(all_visits$Group))
  new_visits <- all_visits %>%
    filter(Visit %in% c("NEW PATIENT VISIT", "NPV TELEHEALTH"))

  # Rank by ALL new visits; only the density calculation requires usable ages.
  group_counts <- data.frame(
    Group = group_levels,
    N_new = as.integer(table(factor(new_visits$Group, levels = group_levels)))
  ) %>%
    arrange(desc(N_new), Group)

  if (nrow(group_counts) != 21L) {
    stop("Expected 21 indication groups; found ", nrow(group_counts),
         ". Check the values in Indication.Group.")
  }

  cohort <- new_visits %>% filter(is.finite(Age), Age >= 0)
  if (nrow(cohort) == 0L) stop("No new visits with usable ages.")

  cohort$Indication[
    is.na(cohort$Indication) | cohort$Indication %in% c("", "NA", "?")
  ] <- "Unspecified"
  cohort$Outcome[
    is.na(cohort$Outcome) | cohort$Outcome %in% c("", "NA")
  ] <- "Negative"

  unknown <- setdiff(unique(cohort$Outcome[cohort$Tested]), result_order)
  if (length(unknown)) {
    stop("Unexpected Classification value(s): ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "))
  }

  # Common age axis and bandwidth across every panel.
  age_limits <- c(0, max(100, ceiling(max(cohort$Age) / 10) * 10 + 10))
  age_grid <- seq(age_limits[1], age_limits[2], length.out = 600)
  dx <- age_grid[2] - age_grid[1]

  # Support both current and older ggplot2 legend-position syntax.
  inside_legend_theme <- if (utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "3.5.0") {
    theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.98, legend_y))
  } else {
    theme(legend.position = c(0.98, legend_y))
  }

  make_panel <- function(group_name, rank_number, total_new) {
    d <- cohort[cohort$Group == group_name, , drop = FALSE]
    n_all <- nrow(d)
    n_tested <- sum(d$Tested)
    panel_title <- sprintf("%s. %s", LETTERS[rank_number],
                           gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", group_name))

    if (n_all == 0L) {
      return(
        ggplot() +
          annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0,
                   label = paste0("New visits: ", fmt_n(total_new),
                                  "\nNo new visits with usable ages"), size = 3) +
          labs(title = panel_title) + theme_void() +
          theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
      )
    }

    ind_counts <- sort(table(d$Indication), decreasing = TRUE)
    ind_order <- names(ind_counts)  # Most common band is nearest the center.
    major <- ind_order[as.numeric(ind_counts) / n_all > label_threshold]
    has_other <- any(!ind_order %in% major)

    # Internal keys distinguish the combined legend entry from real labels.
    major_keys <- paste0("ind:", major)
    other_key <- "other:all"
    ind_colors <- setNames("#00441B", other_key)
    if (length(major)) {
      ind_colors <- c(ind_colors, setNames(
        grDevices::colorRampPalette(
          c("#238B45", "#D9F0A3"), space = "Lab"
        )(length(major)), major_keys
      ))
    }

    # Legend runs top-to-bottom: other, least common named ... most common.
    ind_breaks <- c(if (has_other) other_key, rev(major_keys))
    ind_labels <- c(
      setNames("All other indications", other_key),
      setNames(vapply(major, function(g) {
        sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", g),
                100 * as.numeric(ind_counts[g]) / n_all)
      }, character(1)), major_keys)
    )

    # Each record contributes area 1/n_all to the upper density.
    kernels <- outer(age_grid, d$Age, function(x, mu) {
      stats::dnorm(x, mean = mu, sd = bandwidth_years)
    })
    kernel_areas <- dx * (colSums(kernels) -
      (kernels[1, ] + kernels[nrow(kernels), ]) / 2)
    kernels <- sweep(kernels, 2, kernel_areas, "/") / n_all

    make_ribbons <- function(groups, group_order, mirror = FALSE) {
      base <- numeric(length(age_grid))
      layers <- vector("list", length(group_order))
      for (i in seq_along(group_order)) {
        height <- rowSums(kernels[, which(groups == group_order[i]), drop = FALSE])
        top <- base + height
        layers[[i]] <- data.frame(
          Age = age_grid, Group = group_order[i],
          ymin = if (mirror) -top else base,
          ymax = if (mirror) -base else top
        )
        base <- top
      }
      bind_rows(layers)
    }

    upper <- make_ribbons(d$Indication, ind_order)
    upper$Fill <- ifelse(upper$Group %in% major,
                         paste0("ind:", upper$Group), other_key)
    lower <- make_ribbons(ifelse(d$Tested, d$Outcome, NA_character_),
                          result_order, mirror = TRUE)
    y_limit <- 1.65 * max(upper$ymax, abs(lower$ymin))

    new_label <- if (total_new == n_all) {
      paste0("New visits: ", fmt_n(total_new))
    } else {
      sprintf("New visits: %s (%s with age)", fmt_n(total_new), fmt_n(n_all))
    }

    ggplot() +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = upper,
        aes(Age, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = Fill, group = Group),
        colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        name = "Indication", values = ind_colors,
        breaks = ind_breaks, labels = ind_labels[ind_breaks],
        guide = guide_legend(ncol = 1, byrow = TRUE,
                             override.aes = list(colour = NA))
      ) +
      ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = lower,
        aes(Age, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = Group, group = Group),
        colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = result_colors, guide = "none") +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#42536A", linewidth = 0.4) +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = age_limits,
                         breaks = seq(0, age_limits[2], by = 20),
                         expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
      scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-y_limit, y_limit), clip = "off") +
      labs(
        title = panel_title,
        subtitle = sprintf("%s | Tested: %s (%.1f%%)",
                           new_label, fmt_n(n_tested), 100 * n_tested / n_all),
        x = if (rank_number %% 7L == 0L) "Age at evaluation (years)" else NULL,
        y = NULL
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
      theme(
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#EDF1F4", linewidth = 0.25),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = "#536477"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9),
        legend.justification = c(1, 1), legend.direction = "vertical",
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFFE6", colour = NA),
        legend.key = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),
        legend.key.height = grid::unit(3, "mm"),
        legend.key.width = grid::unit(3, "mm"),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = legend_font_size, lineheight = 0.95),
        legend.margin = margin(3, 3, 3, 3),
        legend.spacing.y = grid::unit(0, "mm"),
        plot.margin = margin(8, 10, 8, 10)
      ) + inside_legend_theme
  }

  panels <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(group_counts)), function(i) {
    make_panel(group_counts$Group[i], i, group_counts$N_new[i])
  })

  # Fill down each column: A-G, then H-N, then O-U.
  panel_grid <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
    panels, ncol = 3, nrow = 7, byrow = FALSE, guides = "keep"
  )

  # Build one results legend separately; no panel contains a results legend.
  legend_data <- data.frame(
    x = seq_along(result_order), y = 1,
    Result = factor(result_order, levels = result_order)
  )
  legend_plot <- ggplot(legend_data, aes(x, y, fill = Result)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_manual(
      name = "Testing result", values = result_colors,
      breaks = result_order, labels = result_labels[result_order], drop = FALSE,
      guide = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE)
    ) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "horizontal",
          legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          legend.key.width = grid::unit(5, "mm"),
          legend.key.height = grid::unit(4, "mm"))

  legend_table <- ggplotGrob(legend_plot)
  legend_indices <- which(grepl("^guide-box", legend_table$layout$name))
  legend_indices <- legend_indices[vapply(
    legend_table$grobs[legend_indices], function(g) inherits(g, "gtable"), logical(1)
  )]
  if (!length(legend_indices)) stop("Could not extract the shared results legend.")
  shared_legend <- legend_table$grobs[[legend_indices[1]]]

  patchwork::wrap_plots(
    panel_grid, patchwork::wrap_elements(full = shared_legend),
    ncol = 1, heights = c(1, 0.025), guides = "keep"
  ) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = "Age distributions across adult genetics indication groups",
      subtitle = paste(
        "New-patient visits: referral indications above; testing results below.",
        "Groups ranked by new-patient count, down each column."
      ),
      caption = paste(
        "Named indications represent >5% of plotted new visits within each group; all others share deep green, with separate bands.",
        "Within each panel, upper area = 1 and lower area = fraction tested. Vertical scales vary across panels.",
        "Ordering uses all new visits, including telehealth. Curves, testing counts, and testing percentages require a usable age.",
        sep = "\n"
      ),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 19),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, colour = "#536477"),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0, colour = "#637588"),
        plot.margin = margin(12, 12, 12, 12)
      )
    )
})

All_Indication_Age_Mirrored
```

## Figure S4 · Patients receiving WES/WGS vs. other genetic tests {#figS4}

<div class="caption"><span class="caplabel">Manuscript legend</span> Each panel shows the distribution of patient characteristics by whether WES/WGS (n = 168) or another genetic test (n = 4,077) was sent. (A–B) clinical indication group; (C–D) EHR-reported race; (E–F) EHR-reported sex; (G–H) financial class; (I) age at visit. Chi-square comparisons for A–H were significant for indication and financial class only; asterisks mark categories over-represented among WES/WGS patients by residual analysis. Age differed by Wilcoxon rank-sum test (p = 3.35e-21), skewing younger in the WES/WGS group.</div>

### S4 A–B · Indication group {#figS4ab}

```{r figs4ab-indication, fig.width=16, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Supplement > Figure S4 · Patients receiving WES/WGS vs. other genetic tests > S4 A–B · Indication group
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.
## Creates : base_levels, final_levels, palette_colors, prep_plot_data, plot_data_all, legend_labels_all, Plot.Indication.Pie, plot_data_wes, legend_labels_wes, Plot.Indication.Pie.WES, Plot.Indication
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# MedGenData (all visits) is built once in the data chunk (see top of notebook).

####### Demographics of Indications for WES/WGS
# Step 1: Define consistent levels and color palette
base_levels <- MedGenData %>%
  count(Indication.Group) %>%
  arrange(n) %>%
  pull(Indication.Group)

final_levels <- c(setdiff(base_levels, "Hypermobility"), "Hypermobility")

palette_colors <- setNames(
  rev(c(stepped2(length(final_levels) - 1), "grey30")),
  rev(final_levels)
)

# Step 2: Helper function to prep data and generate labels
prep_plot_data <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    count(Indication.Group, name = "n") %>%
    complete(Indication.Group = rev(final_levels), fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    mutate(
      perc = n / sum(n),
      Indication.Group = factor(Indication.Group, levels = rev(final_levels)),
      legend_label = paste0(Indication.Group, ", ", round(perc * 100, 2), "%")
    )
}

# Step 3: All testing plot
plot_data_all <- prep_plot_data(MedGenData %>% filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>% filter(!(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS"))))

legend_labels_all <- setNames(plot_data_all$legend_label, plot_data_all$Indication.Group)

Plot.Indication.Pie <- ggplot(plot_data_all, aes(x = "", y = perc, fill = Indication.Group)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(fill = "Indication, % of total") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_colors, labels = legend_labels_all) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
  ggtitle("Indications, All")

# Step 4: WES/WGS-only plot
plot_data_wes <- prep_plot_data(MedGenData %>% filter(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS")))

legend_labels_wes <- setNames(plot_data_wes$legend_label, plot_data_wes$Indication.Group)

Plot.Indication.Pie.WES <- ggplot(plot_data_wes, aes(x = "", y = perc, fill = Indication.Group)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(fill = "Indication, % of total") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_colors, labels = legend_labels_wes) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
  ggtitle("Indications, WES/WGS")

# Step 5: Combine
Plot.Indication <- Plot.Indication.Pie.WES | Plot.Indication.Pie

# ---- display ----

print(Plot.Indication)
```


<details class="stats">
<summary>Stats for WES/WGS Differences in Indication</summary>

```{r wes-stats-demo-indiation, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Supplement > Figure S4 · Patients receiving WES/WGS vs. other genetic tests > S4 A–B · Indication group
## What    : Chi-square Test: Indication Group vs. Test Type
## Creates : indication_test_table, chisq_matrix, chi_test, chi_summary
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare data
indication_test_table <- MedGenData %>%
  filter(!is.na(Indication.Group), Indication.Group != "") %>%
  mutate(WES_WGS = ifelse(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS"), "WES/WGS", ifelse(   !(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS")) & Testing_Sent == "Yes", "Other",  "Neither"    ))) %>%
  filter(WES_WGS != "Neither") %>%
  count(WES_WGS, Indication.Group) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WES_WGS, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

# Convert to matrix
chisq_matrix <- as.matrix(indication_test_table[, c("WES/WGS", "Other")])
rownames(chisq_matrix) <- indication_test_table$Indication.Group

# Perform chi-square test
chi_test <- chisq.test(chisq_matrix)

# Extract test statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value
chi_summary <- data.frame(
  Statistic = round(chi_test$statistic, 2),
  `Degrees of Freedom` = chi_test$parameter,
  `p-value` = formatC(chi_test$p.value, digits = 2, format = "e")
)

datatable(
  chi_summary,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Chi-square Test: Indication Group vs. Test Type",
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE)
)
```
</details>

<details class="stats">
<summary>ChiSq Residuals for WES/WGS Differences in Indication</summary>

```{r wes-stats-demo-indiation-bubble-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=4, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Supplement > Figure S4 · Patients receiving WES/WGS vs. other genetic tests > S4 A–B · Indication group
## What    : Fits the model / runs the test described in the section heading and returns a formatted table.
## Creates : indication_table, chisq
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare contingency table
indication_table <- MedGenData %>%
  mutate(WES_Group = ifelse(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS"), "WES/WGS", ifelse(   !(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS")) & Testing_Sent == "Yes", "Other",  "Neither"    ))) %>%
  filter(WES_Group != "Neither") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Indication.Group), !is.na(WES_Group)) %>%
  count(Indication.Group, WES_Group) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WES_Group, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Indication.Group") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Run chi-square test
chisq <- chisq.test(indication_table)

# Plot Pearson residuals

corrplot(
  t(chisq$residuals),  # <- transpose here
  is.cor = FALSE,
  col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(200),
  tl.col = "black",
  tl.cex = 0.8,
  cl.cex = 0.8,
  title = "Pearson Residuals of Chi-square Test (Rotated)",
  mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0)
)
```

```{r figs4cd-race, fig.width=16, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Analysis / plot]  Supplement > Figure S4 · Patients receiving WES/WGS vs. other genetic tests > S4 C–D · Race
## What    : Builds and prints the plot for this section.

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Race Pie Chart
# Define all expected post-mutation race categories (from your data)
race_levels <- c(
  "White",
  "Unknown/Other",
  "Black or African American",
  "Hispanic or Latino of any race",
  "Asian",
  "American Indian or Alaskan Native",
  "Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander"
)

# Assign distinct colors using RColorBrewer
race_colors <- setNames(
  colorRampPalette( brewer.pal(8,"Set1"))(12)[c(2:4, 7:11)],
  race_levels
)

# Function to prepare race data for plotting
prep_race_data <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    filter(!is.na(RACE), RACE != "?", RACE != "NA") %>%
    mutate(RACE = factor(RACE, levels = race_levels)) %>%
    group_by(RACE) %>%
    count(name = "n") %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      perc = n / sum(n),
      legend_label = paste0(RACE, ", ", round(perc * 100, 1), "%"),
      text_y = cumsum(perc) - perc / 2
    )
}

# Prepare data
race_all <- prep_race_data(MedGenData %>% filter(Testing_Sent == "Yes") %>% filter(!(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS"))))

race_wes <- prep_race_data(MedGenData %>% filter(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS")))

# Build label maps for consistent legend entries
race_all_labels <- setNames(race_all$legend_label, race_all$RACE)

race_wes_labels <- setNames(race_wes$legend_label, race_wes$RACE)

# Plot: All patients
Plot.Demo.Race.all <- ggplot(race_all, aes(x = "", y = perc, fill = RACE)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    fill = "Self Reported Race,\n% of total",
    title = "All Patients"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = race_colors,
    labels = race_all_labels
  )

# Plot: WES/WGS patients
Plot.Demo.Race.wes <- ggplot(race_wes, aes(x = "", y = perc, fill = RACE)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    fill = "Self Reported Race,\n% of total",
    title = "WES/WGS Patients"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = race_colors,
    labels = race_wes_labels
  )

Race.Wes.Compare <- Plot.Demo.Race.wes |Plot.Demo.Race.all

# ---- display ----

print(Race.Wes.Compare)
```

```{r wes-stats-demo-race, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Supplement > Figure S4 · Patients receiving WES/WGS vs. other genetic tests > S4 C–D · Race
## What    : Chi-square Test Summary: Race vs. WES/WGS Testing
## Creates : race_test_table, chisq_matrix_race, chi_test_race, race_chisq_summary
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 1: Prepare race test table
race_test_table <- MedGenData %>%
  filter(!is.na(RACE), RACE != "?", RACE != "NA") %>%
  mutate(WES_WGS = ifelse(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS"), "WES/WGS", ifelse(   !(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS")) & Testing_Sent == "Yes", "Other",  "Neither"    ))) %>%
  filter(WES_WGS != "Neither") %>%
  count(WES_WGS, RACE) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WES_WGS, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

# Step 2: Convert to matrix
chisq_matrix_race <- as.matrix(race_test_table[, c("WES/WGS", "Other")])
rownames(chisq_matrix_race) <- race_test_table$RACE

# Step 3: Perform chi-square test
chi_test_race <- chisq.test(chisq_matrix_race)

# Step 4: Output chi-square test summary as datatable
race_chisq_summary <- data.frame(
  `Chi-squared` = round(chi_test_race$statistic, 2),
  `df` = chi_test_race$parameter,
  `p-value` = formatC(chi_test_race$p.value, digits = 2, format = "e"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

DT::datatable(
  race_chisq_summary,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Chi-square Test Summary: Race vs. WES/WGS Testing",
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE)
)
```

```{r wes-stats-demo-sex, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Supplement > Figure S4 · Patients receiving WES/WGS vs. other genetic tests > S4 E–F · Sex
## What    : Logistic Regression: Odds of Receiving WES/WGS vs Other by Gender
## Creates : gender_reg_data, gender_logit, gender_or_table
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare data for logistic regression
gender_reg_data <- MedGenData %>%
  mutate(WES_WGS = ifelse(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS"), "WES/WGS", ifelse(   !(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS")) & Testing_Sent == "Yes", "Other",  "Neither"    ))) %>%
  filter(WES_WGS != "Neither") %>%
  filter(!is.na(GENDER), GENDER != "?", GENDER != "X") %>%
  mutate(
    WES_WGS = ifelse(WES_WGS == "WES/WGS", 1, 0),
    GENDER = factor(GENDER)
  ) %>%
  distinct(PAT_MRN_ID, GENDER, WES_WGS, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Run logistic regression (reference: first level alphabetically, e.g., Female)
gender_logit <- glm(WES_WGS ~ GENDER, data = gender_reg_data, family = binomial())

# Get odds ratio, CI, and p-value for GENDER
gender_or_table <- broom::tidy(gender_logit, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    `OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
    `p-value` = formatC(p.value, format = "e", digits = 2)
  ) %>%
  select(Predictor = term, `OR (95% CI)`, `p-value`)

# Show in a datatable
DT::datatable(
  gender_or_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Logistic Regression: Odds of Receiving WES/WGS vs Other by Gender",
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE)
)
```

```{r wes-stats-demo-insurance, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 1: Prepare insurance test table
insurance_test_table <- MedGenData %>%
  filter(!is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NULL") %>%
  mutate(
    FINANCIAL_CLASS = case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",

      TRUE ~ FINANCIAL_CLASS
    )) %>%
  mutate(WES_WGS = ifelse(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS"), "WES/WGS", ifelse(   !(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS")) & Testing_Sent == "Yes", "Other",  "Neither"    ))) %>%

# Step 2: Convert to matrix
chisq_matrix_insurance <- as.matrix(insurance_test_table[, c("WES/WGS", "Other")])
rownames(chisq_matrix_insurance) <- insurance_test_table$FINANCIAL_CLASS

# Step 3: Perform chi-square test
chi_test_insurance <- chisq.test(chisq_matrix_insurance)

# Summarize chi-square test result
```

```{r wes-stats-demo-insurance-bubble-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=4, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Supplement > Figure S4 · Patients receiving WES/WGS vs. other genetic tests > S4 G–H · Insurance class
## What    : Fits the model / runs the test described in the section heading and returns a formatted table.
## Creates : insurance_table, chisq_insurance
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare contingency table
insurance_table <- MedGenData %>%
  filter(!is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), FINANCIAL_CLASS != "NULL") %>%
  mutate(
    FINANCIAL_CLASS = case_when(
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Blue Cross", "Blue Shield", "Commercial", "Managed Care") ~ "Commercial",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Medicare", "Managed Medicare") ~ "Medicare",
      FINANCIAL_CLASS %in% c("Managed Medicaid", "Medicaid (MA)") ~ "Medicaid",
      TRUE ~ FINANCIAL_CLASS
    )) %>%
    mutate(WES_Group = ifelse(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS"), "WES/WGS", ifelse(   !(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS")) & Testing_Sent == "Yes", "Other",  "Neither"    ))) %>%
  filter(WES_Group != "Neither") %>%
  filter(!is.na(FINANCIAL_CLASS), !is.na(WES_Group)) %>%
  count(FINANCIAL_CLASS, WES_Group) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WES_Group, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("FINANCIAL_CLASS") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Run chi-square test
chisq_insurance <- chisq.test(insurance_table)

# Visualize Pearson residuals
corrplot(
  t(chisq_insurance$residuals),  # transpose to rotate
  is.cor = FALSE,
  col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(200),
  tl.col = "black",
  tl.cex = 0.8,
  cl.cex = 0.8,
  title = "Pearson Residuals of Chi-square Test: Insurance vs WES/WGS",
  mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0)
)
```

```{r wes-stats-demo-age, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## [Statistics]  Supplement > Figure S4 · Patients receiving WES/WGS vs. other genetic tests > S4 I · Age
## What    : Age by Testing Category. Wilcoxon rank-sum test compares WES/WGS vs. All Other Visits.
## Creates : age_test_data, wilcox_test, p_value, group_stats, summary_table
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare data
age_test_data <- MedGenData %>%
  filter(!is.na(VISIT_AGE), VISIT_AGE >= 10, VISIT_AGE <= 90) %>%
    mutate(CategoryWES = ifelse(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS"), "WES/WGS", ifelse(   !(Test.Category %in% c("WES", "WGS")) & Testing_Sent == "Yes", "All Other Visits",  "Neither"    ))) %>%
  filter(CategoryWES != "Neither")

# Wilcoxon test
wilcox_test <- wilcox.test(
  VISIT_AGE ~ CategoryWES,
  data = age_test_data
)
p_value <- wilcox_test$p.value

# Summarize group stats
group_stats <- age_test_data %>%
  group_by(CategoryWES) %>%
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    Mean_Age = mean(VISIT_AGE, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Age = median(VISIT_AGE, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Add p-value to both rows (for clarity)
summary_table <- group_stats %>%
  mutate(`Wilcoxon p-value` = formatC(p_value, digits = 2, format = "e"))

datatable(
  summary_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Age by Testing Category. Wilcoxon rank-sum test compares WES/WGS vs. All Other Visits.",
  options = list(dom = 't', paging = FALSE)
)
```
